name: Prof. Amb. Dr Abhnash K Bains
summary: Prof. Amb. Dr Abhnash K. Bains has dedicated over 30 years to mental health advocacy, cultural dialogue, and philanthropy. As founder of Ishkama Global Change CIC, Ishkama Radio, and IGC Magazine, she champions emotional wellbeing and women's empowerment, creating supportive public platforms that celebrate inspiring changemakers and foster social inclusion.
fullText:
Prof. Amb. Dr Abhnash K. Bains is a philanthropist and community advocate whose work reflects a longstanding commitment to social wellbeing, cultural understanding, inclusion and the empowerment of individuals and communities. Through her continued involvement in charitable and community initiatives, she has worked to raise awareness of important social issues, encourage meaningful dialogue and create opportunities for people to connect, share their experiences and support one another.
As the Founder of Ishkama Global Change CIC, she has championed community-focused initiatives that promote mental health awareness, emotional wellbeing, women’s empowerment, social inclusion and positive social change. Her work recognises the importance of creating supportive communities in which people feel heard, valued and encouraged to contribute. She has consistently advocated for greater understanding of mental health and the need to approach individuals and their lived experiences with compassion, dignity and respect.
Through IGC Magazine, she has helped provide a platform for sharing inspiring personal journeys, community initiatives and stories that bring attention to individuals working towards a positive difference in society. Through Ishkama Radio, she has further supported conversations that encourage awareness, understanding and the sharing of diverse voices and experiences. These platforms reflect her commitment to using communication as a means of connecting people, highlighting social causes and encouraging wider community participation.
Her work also encompasses the promotion of cultural understanding, the recognition of women's contributions and the encouragement of collaborative efforts that benefit society. She believes that meaningful change is achieved not only through large initiatives but also through consistent acts of service, raising awareness, listening to others and creating spaces where people can support one another.
Through her ongoing community engagement, Prof. Amb. Dr Abhnash K. Bains continues to uphold the values of compassion, service, inclusion and collective responsibility. Her contribution reflects a belief that a stronger society is built when people are given a voice, communities are supported and individuals are encouraged to become part of positive change.

name: Aishwarya Kumar
org: Lions Club of Romford / Community Governance
summary: Aishwarya Kumar is a business owner, educator, school governor, and Chair of the Hornchurch & Upminster CLP. Recipient of the Mayor’s Civic Pride Award, she coordinates school vision screening programmes, sponsors community bleed safety kits, supports food banks, and provides remote phonics education to rural pupils in India.
fullText:
I am Aishwarya Kumar, an IT engineer who transitioned into teaching and is also a businesswoman. For the past 12 years, I have run a granite business in London. I am also a devoted wife and mother in a family of four, supported by my loving husband and our two children.
Alongside my professional and business activities, I am a community volunteer, charity leader, school governor and Chair of the Hornchurch & Upminster Constituency Labour Party (CLP), based in Havering. With the support of my family, I have been able to dedicate time to serving the local community, supporting charitable initiatives and contributing to local civic and educational life.
Through my role as Secretary of the Lions Club of Romford, I have supported initiatives benefiting food banks, disadvantaged children, community safety and health awareness. I am also leading a major school vision-screening project, helping to identify children who may require further eye care and supporting early intervention for potential vision problems.
My community service includes donating Christmas gifts to disadvantaged children and families, sponsoring bleed kits to support emergency preparedness and community safety, and teaching phonics to rural children in India to help improve their early literacy and reading skills. I have also supported local families, promoted early health awareness, assisted vulnerable members of the community and brought people together through volunteering and charitable activities.
As a school governor, I contribute to the governance and development of the school, supporting its commitment to providing a positive, inclusive and supportive environment for pupils, families and staff. As Chair of the Hornchurch & Upminster CLP, I also help coordinate local party activities, encourage community engagement and support members and residents across the constituency.
In recognition of my contribution to the local community, I was honoured to receive the Mayor’s Civic Award, which was published in the Havering Daily.
Havering Daily article: [https://thehaveringdaily.co.uk/2026/03/26/lions-club-of-romford-celebrated-with-civic-pride-award-for-exceptional-community-service/]

name: Amarjit Jammu
org: Public Service / Civic Leadership & Digital Inclusion
summary: Amarjit Jammu has dedicated over six decades to public service, community governance, and social welfare. A former elected Councillor, School Governor, and UNISON committee member, she has championed digital literacy programmes for elderly citizens, organized soup kitchen relief, and served as primary caregiver for her grandchild with complex needs, embodying lifelong selfless seva.
fullText:
From an early age, I was introduced to the value of helping others by my mother, who took me with her to distribute essential school supplies to vulnerable children, ensuring they had the resources needed to learn and succeed. Those experiences instilled in me a lifelong commitment to service and community support.
For more than six decades, I have dedicated my time to serving others through volunteering, charitable initiatives, public service, and community leadership. My work has included supporting food banks and soup kitchens, children's charities, elderly residents, carers, and vulnerable families. I have also worked extensively to reduce digital exclusion, helping older residents develop confidence with technology and access essential services, ensuring that no one is left behind.
Alongside my voluntary work, I have served as a School Governor, member of governing bodies, elected Councillor, and public servant. Through these roles, I have advocated for local residents, supported vulnerable individuals, and contributed to improving services and opportunities within the community.
I also took early retirement to become the primary carer for my grandson, who lives with Leber's Congenital Amaurosis and Type 1 diabetes. This responsibility has further strengthened my commitment to compassion, resilience, and supporting others through life's challenges.
Throughout my life, I have been guided by honesty, integrity, kindness, and the principle of Seva, selfless service. Whether through public service, voluntary work, leadership, or personal caring responsibilities, I have consistently sought to make a positive difference and help create stronger, more inclusive communities.
Key Contributions
•Over 60 years of community service and volunteering.
•Support for food banks, soup kitchens, children's charities, and vulnerable families.
•Championing digital inclusion for elderly and vulnerable residents.
•Service as a School Governor and member of governing bodies.
•Elected Councillor advocating for local communities.
•Long career in public service, supporting people through essential services.
•Full-time caring responsibilities for a grandchild with complex needs.
•Lifelong commitment to Seva, inclusion, compassion, and community empowerment.

fullText:

name: Anita Matharoo
summary: Anita Matharoo has dedicated many years to community development and cultural preservation through grassroots broadcasting. Using community radio as an inclusive vehicle for public education and social dialogue, she amplifies community voices, raises awareness on social welfare, and leads outreach programmes supporting women, children, and Panjabi linguistic heritage.
fullText:
For many years, I have dedicated my time, energy, and passion to serving and supporting the local community, working tirelessly to bring people together, strengthen community connections, and create opportunities for people to thrive. Community service has always been at the heart of everything I do, and I have consistently championed initiatives that promote inclusion, wellbeing, cultural understanding, and social cohesion.
A significant part of my work has focused on promoting and preserving Panjabi culture, language, and heritage. I am passionate about ensuring that these traditions continue to be celebrated and passed on to future generations, helping people maintain a strong sense of identity and pride in their cultural roots.
Through my long-standing involvement in community radio, I have provided a trusted platform for information, education, discussion, and cultural expression. Community radio has enabled me to reach and engage diverse audiences, raise awareness of important local issues, highlight community achievements, support local organisations, and connect individuals who may otherwise feel isolated. By giving a voice to local people and sharing stories that matter, I have helped strengthen community engagement and foster a greater sense of belonging.
I am also deeply committed to supporting women and children within the community. Through community outreach, events, and local initiatives, I have worked to empower women, encourage confidence and participation, and create opportunities for personal growth and social connection. I have also supported children and young people by promoting cultural awareness, education, creativity, and community involvement, helping them develop the skills and confidence needed to succeed.
My dedication to community service, cultural preservation, and social inclusion has enabled me to make a meaningful and lasting contribution to the lives of many people. I remain committed to using my experience, passion, and community networks to support, inspire, and empower others, helping to build stronger, more connected, and more resilient communities for future generations.
I believe that strong communities are built through connection, understanding, and service, and I am proud to continue dedicating my time to making a positive difference in the lives of others.

name: Dr Anjali Ghosh
summary: Dr Anjali Ghosh is a distinguished molecular biologist, academic course leader, and community organizer. For over 20 years, she has guided the Wimbledon Cultural Association, earning national awards for UK cultural celebrations. She also launched the Indian Heritage and Cultural Association youth platform, fostering STEM capabilities, language skills, and heritage among British Indian youth.
fullText:
Dr Anjali Ghosh is a distinguished molecular biologist and a registered biomedical scientist-turned-academician. Her work initially focused on cancer cell lines, contributing valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying cancer. Her scientific journey expanded as they transitioned into bacterial genomics, where she has continued to push the boundaries of research and innovation in the field. Over the years, Anjali has led pioneering work that has greatly advanced our understanding of microbial genetics.
In addition to their groundbreaking scientific contributions, Anjali has played an instrumental role in shaping the next generation of biomedical scientists. As the course leader of a successful degree program, she has dedicated herself to mentoring students and fostering a new wave of talent in the biomedical sciences.

name: Anjali Singhal
org: OneSlough Volunteer of the Year / Community Health
summary: Anjali Singhal is a dedicated Slough community organizer who mobilized volunteers to prepare and deliver 250 daily meals to key workers and vulnerable families throughout the pandemic. Her ongoing weekly health awareness seminars and proactive screening clinics earned her the OneSlough Volunteer of the Year Award.
fullText:
Since 2011, I have been dedicated to volunteering and supporting families across Slough, driven by a passion for improving lives and strengthening my community.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, I brought together a group of women to prepare, package and help deliver 250 meals daily to vulnerable individuals, families in need and our brave key workers. This initiative was about more than providing food; it was about bringing people together, offering support and ensuring that those who needed help most felt cared for during an incredibly challenging time.
As the pandemic eased, my commitment to the community remained unwavering. I began organising weekly community talks to raise awareness and educate residents on important issues, including health, education and safety. I also worked to create welcoming spaces where community members could access health checks, learn more about their bodies and take a proactive approach to their health and wellbeing.
In recognition of my dedication and impact, I was honoured to receive the Volunteer of the Year Award from OneSlough for championing health and wellbeing.

name: Dr (Prof) Arpita Ray
summary: Dr Arpita Ray is a Consultant in Reproductive Medicine and IVF specialist renowned for two decades of impactful civic leadership. She founded EssexIndians Charity, Maitreya Bengali Club, and Heritage Connect CIC, spearheading large-scale cultural festivals, language classes, and youth impact initiatives. An adventurous community role model, she also completed the Three Peaks Challenge in a traditional saree.
fullText:
Dr Arpita Ray
Dr Arpita Ray is a Consultant in Reproductive Medicine and IVF Specialist in the United Kingdom, whose professional excellence is matched by an unwavering commitment to community service, cultural preservation, youth empowerment, and social cohesion.
Alongside a distinguished medical career, Dr Ray has dedicated over two decades to creating opportunities that bring communities together through education, culture, health, and the performing arts. Her work has inspired thousands of children, young adults, and families across the UK, making her one of the most recognised community leaders within the British Indian and British Bengali communities.
She is the Founder Trustee of EssexIndians Charity, a leading community organisation established to celebrate Indian heritage while promoting integration, volunteering, and intercultural understanding. Under her leadership, EssexIndians has grown into a respected platform delivering large-scale cultural festivals, educational initiatives, health awareness programmes, youth development projects, and charitable fundraising activities.
Recognising the importance of preserving language and identity among younger generations, Dr Ray founded the Maitreya Bengali Club, where she has voluntarily taught Bengali to British-born children for many years. Through innovative teaching and cultural engagement, she has enabled hundreds of young people to reconnect with their linguistic and cultural heritage.
A passionate advocate for theatre and the performing arts, Dr Ray founded the Uttorsuri Generation Next Festival (2015–2025), nurturing children and adults in acting, stagecraft, and performance. The festival has produced numerous acclaimed productions while providing a creative platform for emerging artists and encouraging confidence, teamwork, and artistic excellence.
Continuing her vision of promoting heritage through the arts, she established Heritage Connect CIC in 2024 and launched Parampara Utsav, an annual celebration dedicated to Indian classical music, drama, dance, literature, and cultural traditions. The festival has become an important platform for artists and audiences to celebrate and preserve South Asian heritage in the United Kingdom.
Dr Ray is also a Founder Trustee of the United Kingdom Bengali Convention (UKBC) Charity, where she has played an instrumental role in developing youth engagement programmes and supporting the Convention’s drama festival since 2021, encouraging wider participation of young people in cultural and community life.
As a Director of Basildon Side by Side, she has championed community cohesion and wellbeing through innovative partnerships with Basildon Council and Active Essex. She has successfully initiated and led projects such as Dance for Happiness and Fitness is Happiness, improving physical health, mental wellbeing, and social connectedness among diverse communities.
In 2026, Dr Ray conceived and directed the Youth Impact Award, a national initiative recognising exceptional young people making positive contributions to society. The inaugural awards ceremony was held at the UK Parliament, providing a prestigious national platform to celebrate youth leadership, volunteering, creativity, and community service.
An accomplished fundraiser, Dr Ray has raised significant support for numerous charitable organisations and community initiatives throughout her career. Her belief that leadership is demonstrated through action has inspired many to volunteer, contribute, and actively engage in community development.
Beyond her professional and voluntary work, Dr Ray is known for her adventurous spirit and her commitment to promoting women’s empowerment and cultural identity. In 2018, she became one of the first British Asian Bengali women to complete a solo Land’s End to John O’Groats (LEJOG) driving challenge. In 2025, she completed the National Three Peaks Challenge wearing a traditional Indian saree, symbolising that cultural heritage and modern achievement can proudly coexist.
Her contributions have been recognised through several prestigious honours. In 2023, she received the Community Champion Award from the United Kingdom Bengali Convention (UKBC) in recognition of her outstanding service to the community. In 2026, she was honoured with the IIW She Inspires Award, celebrating her inspirational leadership, commitment to women’s empowerment, and exceptional contribution to society.
Whether working as a fertility specialist, mentoring young people, directing theatre productions, preserving language and culture, or building stronger communities through partnership and innovation, Dr Arpita Ray continues to lead with compassion, vision, and purpose.
Her enduring mission is to empower future generations, celebrate cultural diversity, improve community wellbeing, and leave a lasting legacy of inclusion, creativity, and service.

name: Chinu Kishore
org: Luitporia Nasoni / United Assam Association UK
summary: Chinu Kishore is a prominent cultural leader and founder of Luitporia Nasoni, dedicated to preserving and celebrating Assamese heritage, Sattriya dance, and Bihu traditions in the United Kingdom. Serving as Secretary of the United Assam Association UK, she has showcased Assam's rich cultural legacy on esteemed platforms, including the UK Parliament and the Nehru Centre, bridging generational connections across the diaspora.
fullText:
Chinu Kishore is a prominent UK-based cultural leader, community organiser and founder of Luitporia Nasoni, dedicated to promoting Assamese heritage, Sattriya, Bihu and the rich cultural traditions of Assam in the United Kingdom.
She serves as Secretary of the United Assam Association UK (UAAUK) and has played a leading role in bringing Assamese culture and heritage to prominent platforms across the UK, including the British Parliament and the Nehru Centre, London.
When it comes to Assam’s name, cultural identity and community leadership in the UK, Chinu Kishore is a name that comes first. Her tireless efforts have helped raise the profile of Assam, its traditions and its people, while creating meaningful opportunities for younger generations to connect with and carry forward their heritage.
Through Luitporia Nasoni, her vision is centred on promoting Assamese heritage, connecting generations and reducing isolation. Her work encompasses cultural programmes, community engagement, promotion of Sattriya and traditional arts, and initiatives that strengthen the connection between Assam and the Assamese diaspora in the UK.
Her contribution to Assamese culture has received recognition, including the Femina Global Cultural Leader Award, further reflecting her commitment to cultural promotion and community leadership.
Chinu Kishore continues to be a passionate voice for Assam in the UK, working to ensure that Assamese culture is not only preserved but proudly represented on some of the UK’s most respected platforms.

name: Ms Chiragi Solanki
summary: Ms Chiragi Solanki has dedicated nearly 30 years to voluntary service, arts education, and cultural outreach in Leeds. An elected committee member at Leeds Hindu Mandir and founder of Northern England's largest Indian dance academy, she has trained thousands of students. Through Haqooq, she delivers free performing arts programmes for special educational needs institutions.
fullText:
For nearly 30 years in Leeds, I have proudly dedicated myself to voluntary community service. For the past 18 years, I have served as an elected committee member of Leeds Hindu Mandir, organising major cultural events and festivals while managing its Facebook community of more than 6,000 members. I also serve as a Hindu Faith Representative with Leeds City Council/Leeds Faith Forum and as the Yorkshire representative for Vihangam Yoga, where I organise free meditation and yoga sessions to promote wellbeing within the community.
Through Haqooq, I deliver free Indian arts, culture and dance programmes for special educational needs schools and colleges. The organisation has recently been nominated for the King's Award for Voluntary Service. I also regularly organise fundraising events in support of the Lord Mayor's Charity, working closely with Leeds Civic Hall to help raise funds for important local causes. I have had the honour of meeting His Majesty King Charles III.
Professionally, I am a qualified dance teacher and the founder of North England's largest Bollywood and Indian dance school. For more than 30 years, I have trained thousands of students, produced large-scale cultural productions, and had the privilege of performing on some of the UK's biggest stages alongside internationally renowned Bollywood celebrities. Throughout my career, I have remained committed to supporting charities, mentoring young people, and championing community initiatives, while proudly raising my son as a single mother for over 15 years.

name: Dalia Banerjee
org: Indian Bengalis in UK (IBUK) / Cultural Community Leadership
summary: Dalia Banerjee is an engineer, trekker, and the Founder & Administrator of Indian Bengalis in UK (IBUK), connecting over 8,000 members, 90+ Durga Puja committees, and numerous Bengali organisations across England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. She has dedicated years to promoting Bengali cultural heritage and community spirit through signature initiatives such as the UK Durga Pujo Map, Pujo Porikroma, Bengali language programmes, community picnics, and cultural festivals like Mishti Puraan supporting charitable causes.
fullText:
I'm the Founder & Administrator of Indian Bengalis in UK (IBUK), the first Indian Bengali community connecting people across England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, with 8,000+ members, 90+ Durga Puja committees and countless Bengali organisations across the UK.
I've spent years promoting Bengali culture and community spirit through initiatives including Durga Pujo Map of the UK, Pujo Porikroma, Bengali language programmes, family events and an open-air Choruibhati-style picnic.
I've also organised community celebrations such as Mishti Puraan, bringing people together through Bengali food, culture and charitable giving in support of national and international charities.
An engineer by profession and trekker by passion, I bring creativity, organisation, attention to detail and community spirit to everything I undertake. My adventures have taken me to Kilimanjaro and Everest Base Camp.

name: Debbani Ghosh
org: Association of Blind Asians (ABA) / Grace and Care
summary: Debbani Ghosh has served since 2006 as CEO of the Association of Blind Asians in Leeds, delivering culturally tailored support to over 1,600 visually impaired individuals and their carers annually. She co-founded Grace and Care, a community kitchen providing thousands of meals to homeless people, while serving as a prominent champion for diversity and the arts in West Yorkshire.
fullText:
Since 2006, Debbani has served as the CEO of the Association of Blind Asians (ABA) in Leeds, providing crucial, culturally specific support to blind and visually impaired individuals from ethnic minority backgrounds. She is actively involved with various community services in Leeds, ensuring that equality and inclusion are at the heart of her work.
Debbani brings over 20 years of dedicated leadership, community engagement, and operational excellence within the third sector. She is widely recognised across West Yorkshire for her strong commitment to supporting marginalised, minoritised and vulnerable communities.
The charity supports approximately 1,600 people each year from diverse communities and provides numerous community awareness sessions. It also delivers 500plus one-on-one support sessions to those with sight loss and their carers each year. Debbani is a passionate community leader dedicated to creating meaningful opportunities for individuals and communities to thrive. Through her collaborative approach, she has demonstrated outstanding leadership by bringing people together, fostering inclusion, and driving initiatives that create lasting social impact.
Additionally, she runs her own community kitchen Grace and Care, co-founded with her husband, to deliver meal support and improve resilience for those who are vulnerable and experiencing homelessness. So far, she has distributed 7,000 meals and 1,700 food bags over the last five years.
Furthermore, Debbani is a cultural advocate and has participated in numerous cultural activities in Leeds. She is passionate about dance, the arts, culture, and heritage and is dedicated to making a difference in the community.

name: Deval Gujrati
summary: Deval Gujrati has contributed over eight years of multifaceted community service across Reading and Maidenhead. She has served as Secretary at Reading School, shared traditional vocal performances during temple festivities, and developed fundraising initiatives for Gujarat Samaj Reading. She actively collaborates with the Hindu Education Board and civic organizations to strengthen cultural unity.
fullText:
Deval Gujrati - A versatile volunteer
Serving the community is not about the position you hold—it's about the difference you make.
For over eight years, I have proudly volunteered with a range of community organisations, always believing that a kind heart, dedication, and a willingness to help are what truly matter.
My journey began with the Hindu Society in Maidenhead, followed by serving as Secretary at Reading School for two years, where I helped produce the weekly newsletter and supported many school events. For the past three years, I have volunteered my singing during Navratri celebrations at Reading Hindu Temple. Since 2024, I have been an active volunteer with Gujarat Samaj Reading, helping to introduce new fundraising ideas and took initiatives to bring our community together. More recently, I have also been supporting the Hindu Education Board and IIW.
I am passionate about bringing people together, encouraging new ideas, and giving back to the community that has given me so much.
Thank you for your time. I am always happy to help, so please feel free to reach out anytime. Together, we can continue to build a stronger community.
Best wishes
Deval Gujrati

name: Dina Bhudia
summary: Dina Bhudia has dedicated over 15 years to selfless voluntary community service. She serves as the first and only woman trustee of Sewa UK, Chairperson of VHP North London & Herts, and Head of Pandav Vidhya Shala, a volunteer-led school teaching Indian language, values, and Hinduism to the next generation.
fullText: Dina Bhudia has dedicated over 15 years to selfless voluntary community service. She serves as the first and only woman trustee of Sewa UK, Chairperson of VHP North London & Herts, and Head of Pandav Vidhya Shala, a volunteer-led school teaching Indian language, values, and Hinduism to the next generation.

name: Divya Parakat
summary: Divya Parakat is the Founder of EIWP (Empowering International Women’s Paradise), an expansive network supporting women in realizing their personal and professional aspirations. A seasoned global traveler across more than 85 nations, she brings broad international perspective to her community mentorship. Through EIWP, she champions career progression, personal autonomy, and self-confidence for women, building lasting community empowerment.
fullText: Divya Parakat is the Founder of EIWP (Empowering International Women’s Paradise), a thriving network dedicated to empowering women to achieve personal and professional success. An inspiring traveller and explorer who has visited over 85 countries, she brings a global perspective to her work and leadership. Through EIWP, Divya Parakat is committed to helping women advance their careers, build confidence, and embrace true independence in every aspect of their lives. Her vision, leadership, and dedication continue to inspire women to unlock their potential, pursue their ambitions, and create meaningful, lasting impact.

name: Gayatri Lokhande
summary: Gayatri Lokhande is an entrepreneur, community advocate, and mother of three actively championing traditional Indian craftsmanship and handloom heritage. Through her enterprise Shambhavi Weaves, she supports artisans across India and highlights the cultural significance of traditional textiles. She also engages in grassroots civic and political discourse, advocating for community representation and balanced cultural narratives.
fullText:
I am a working mother of three, a community volunteer, social media influencer, handloom enthusiast, entrepreneur, and an active voice for India and the values I believe in.
Alongside my full-time career and raising three children, I dedicate my time to community service, social media advocacy, and supporting Indian artisans and weavers. I use my platform to speak up for India, challenge misinformation and one-sided narratives, and help build positive counter-narratives that reflect India’s diversity, progress, culture, achievements, and global contribution.
I am also passionate about India’s rich handloom heritage and am the proud owner of Shambhavi Weaves, where I curate and sell handloom pieces while helping to promote and uplift the talented weavers of India. For me, handloom is more than just beautiful textiles it represents generations of skill, tradition, identity, and livelihoods. Through Shambhavi Weaves, I hope to help bring greater appreciation and visibility to the people and craftsmanship behind these incredible fabrics.
My journey has also taken me into politics. I have previously stood as a councillor candidate and remain actively engaged in political and community affairs. That experience gave me a deeper understanding of public service, grassroots issues, representation, and the importance of giving people a voice.

name: Gayatri Shenoy
summary: Gayatri Shenoy is a Principal Technical Analyst with over two decades of technology experience and a dedicated STEM ambassador. She actively coaches junior professionals, students, and women entering tech careers, demystifying engineering fields and promoting equal opportunity. Her decade-plus mentorship work across the UK has fostered confidence and technical growth among emerging female innovators.
fullText:
Gayatri Shenoy is a Tech Ambassador and leader, a Principal Technical Analyst with over 20 years of experience in technology, passionate about innovation, AI and using technology to create positive impact. Beyond her professional career, she is a committed Mentor and STEM advocate, dedicated to encouraging students and women to build confidence, explore technology and realise their potential.
For over a decade, Gayatri Shenoy has been passionately committed to giving back to the community through mentoring, guidance and advocacy, with a particular focus on helping students, young people and women build confidence and explore opportunities in technology.
Her contribution has been driven by a simple belief: talent is everywhere, but access to guidance, encouragement and role models is not always equal. Over the years, Gayatri has dedicated her time to supporting students and aspiring professionals as they navigate education, career choices and the often-daunting first steps into the world of technology.
A significant part of her voluntary work has focused on encouraging greater participation of girls and women in technology, helping to demystify the industry and showing that a technology career can be accessible to people from many different backgrounds. Through mentoring conversations, career guidance and community engagement, she has sought to provide practical encouragement while helping individuals recognise their own strengths and possibilities.
Her approach to mentoring goes beyond simply sharing career advice. She believes in listening, building confidence and helping people develop the courage to take their next step, whether that means choosing a field of study, applying for their first opportunity, returning to a technology career, or simply believing that they belong in the industry.
Alongside supporting women, Gayatri has continued to dedicate time to students and the next generation, sharing knowledge and experience to help them understand the breadth of opportunities available within technology.
For Gayatri, giving back is not a one-time initiative but a long-standing personal commitment. The greatest reward has always been seeing someone gain confidence, discover a new possibility, or take a step towards a future they had not previously imagined for themselves.

name: Geeta Shah
summary: Geeta Shah is the founder of Women to Women (W2W), a voluntary organization she has nurtured for 15 years to support thousands of women across the UK. W2W offers wellness clubs, cultural celebrations, emotional counseling, and charitable drives, providing a trusted network that reduces isolation, promotes Gujarati traditions, and builds lasting female leadership.
fullText:
I am the founder of women to women. It was created 15 years ago to support women.
My Skills, Achievements and Contribution to the Gujarati Community
For almost 15 years, I have dedicated my time, energy and skills to building and developing Women to Women (W2W) into a supportive, active and inclusive community for women.
What began as a safe online space for women has grown into a large community bringing women together through social, cultural, spiritual, health, wellbeing and educational activities. Over the years, I have worked almost entirely on a voluntary basis, driven by a genuine desire to support women, strengthen our community and preserve our Gujarati culture and values.
Leadership & Community Development
I founded and developed Women to Women and have continued to lead and coordinate its growth for nearly 15 years. The organisation has evolved from a Facebook community into a much wider network, with thousands of women connected through our Facebook groups and around 500 women participating through our WhatsApp community and numerous specialist groups.
I have created and coordinated groups covering areas such as:
Health and wellbeing
Walking and exercise
Yoga and meditation
Singing, Bollywood music and bhajans
Cooking and sharing recipes
Cultural and spiritual activities
Social events and celebrations
Day trips and outings
Environmental awareness
Support, friendship and practical advice for women
My role has required continuous leadership, organisation, communication, problem-solving and the ability to bring people together from different backgrounds and generations.
Empowering Women
A central aim of Women to Women has always been to create a safe and welcoming environment where women can share knowledge, experiences, skills and opportunities.
I encourage women to participate rather than remain isolated, and I have helped create opportunities for women to discover new interests, develop confidence, make friendships and contribute their own talents to the community.
I believe strongly that community organisations should not simply organise events; they should help people feel valued, connected and empowered.
Gujarati Culture & Heritage
An important part of my work has been promoting and preserving our Gujarati culture and heritage within the UK.
Through cultural programmes, music, dance, religious and spiritual activities, celebrations and community events, I have helped bring women together and encourage younger generations to remain connected with their Gujarati roots.
I have also worked to highlight inspirational Gujarati women and their contributions to society, helping our community recognise the achievements of women who have made a difference both within Gujarat and internationally.
Fundraising & Charitable Work
From the early years of Women to Women, I introduced fundraising initiatives to support charitable causes. This enabled members to come together not only for their own social and cultural benefit but also to contribute to wider society.
I have organised and supported fundraising activities and encouraged members to use their collective strength to help others.
Events & Project Organisation
Over the years I have organised and coordinated a wide range of activities, including social gatherings, cultural programmes, parties, religious events, day trips, exercise and wellbeing sessions, singing and dance activities and community initiatives.
This has involved:
Planning and coordinating events
Recruiting and motivating volunteers
Communicating with large numbers of members
Managing WhatsApp and social media communities
Coordinating venues, activities and participants
Solving problems as they arise
Promoting events and encouraging participation
Working collaboratively with volunteers and community members
Digital & Communication Skills
I have built and managed large online communities using Facebook and WhatsApp and have learned to use these platforms to communicate, organise activities, share information and bring people together.
Managing numerous WhatsApp groups and a large Facebook community requires constant communication, diplomacy, moderation and an understanding of how to maintain a positive and respectful environment.
My Key Strengths
Through almost 15 years of voluntary community work, I have developed strong skills in:
Leadership – taking an idea and turning it into a functioning community initiative.
Organisation – coordinating multiple activities, groups, events and volunteers.
Communication – communicating effectively with women of different ages, backgrounds and interests.
Community Building – creating connections and encouraging people to participate and support one another.
Empowerment – encouraging women to use their talents, develop confidence and become more involved.
Cultural Awareness – promoting Gujarati heritage, traditions and values while maintaining an inclusive approach.
Problem Solving – dealing with the practical challenges involved in running a large voluntary community.
Volunteer Management – bringing people together and encouraging them to contribute their time and skills.
Creativity & Initiative – continually developing new activities and ideas in response to what the community needs.
My Achievement
My greatest achievement is not any single event or project. It is having built a community that has continued to grow and evolve for almost 15 years.
Women to Women has created friendships, connections, opportunities and a sense of belonging for thousands of women. It has provided a platform where women can share their knowledge, celebrate their culture, support charitable causes, learn from one another and simply know that they are not alone.
I am proud that something I started voluntarily many years ago has developed into a community with such a wide range of activities and such a strong network of women.
I would like to continue using my experience, skills and passion for community development to contribute to the wider Gujarati community in the UK, particularly by encouraging greater participation, empowering women, supporting voluntary initiatives and helping preserve our rich cultural heritage for future generations.

name: Geeta Srivastava
org: Magic Of India / Holi At London
summary: Geeta Srivastava founded the social enterprise Magic Of India, bringing Indian arts, language, and culture to life through school workshops and the flagship 'Holi At London' festival hosting 3,000 guests. She previously established the UK arm of Shaadi.com and served on the board of TiE UK.
fullText:
Outstanding Achievement British Indian Award winner Geeta Srivastava nurtures a social enterprise called Magic Of India aimed at bringing Indian culture, arts and language alive in a fun and engaging way, through classes, school workshops and festive events. One of her flagship events in the year is the widely attended Holi At London, which is a massive community event of 3000 audience.
Prior to this, Geeta as the Country Head. set up and lead the UK arm of www.shaadi.com, online match-making. She ran it for 9 years, building it into a huge UK business and establishing it as a household brand.
Her earlier positions include leading marketing for Mainstream Agencies at Zee TV (UK), including the first-ever Asian Fair drawing 28000 audience.
While her tenure in India she was in Leo Burnett. Then Nexus Equity. Then Lintas. Which then became Lowe Lintass. She successfully ran the advertising and marketing arm for Raymond’s fashion, her team winning multiple awards.
She was also the Director of The Indus Entrepreneurs UK, a business networking organisation.

name: Geetanjali Mirpuri
org: Sadhu Vaswani Centre London / Seva Initiatives
summary: Geetanjali Mirpuri has devoted over 35 years in London to charitable seva guided by the teachings of Dada J. P. Vaswani. Through the Sadhu Vaswani Centre, she helped build the Little Lamps Nursery, participates in the Silver Sunday senior companionship programmes, supports weekly food distribution for homeless individuals, and organizes annual toy drives.
fullText:
My Journey of Seva
I have been in London for over 35 years.
My journey of seva has been deeply shaped by the love, wisdom and teachings of my beloved Guru, Dada J. P. Vaswani, who taught us that true spirituality lies in selfless service and compassion for all.
Through the Sadhu Vaswani Centre London, I have been blessed to serve my community in many ways. One of my most cherished sevas is Little Lamps Nursery, which Dada lovingly inspired us to build, nurturing young lives with love and care. I am also involved in Silver Sunday, bringing joy and companionship to our seniors, and weekly feeding of those experiencing homelessness.
Through our Christmas Toy Drive, weekly Satsang and many other initiatives, my endeavour is simply to spread love, bring hope and make a difference.
I see seva not as something I do, but as a blessing and a way of life—a path Dada taught us to walk with humility, love and compassion.

name: Geetha Morla
org: Milton Keynes Council / Women Empowerment Network UK
summary: Geetha Morla made history as the first Telugu councillor and the first Indian elected to Milton Keynes Council. A pioneering civic leader, she is the Founder and Trustee of Women Empowerment Network UK and serves as Trustee of UKTA, advocating for public engagement, social justice, and representation for the Telugu and wider diaspora.
fullText: Geetha Morla made history as the first Telugu councillor and the first Indian elected to Milton Keynes Council. A pioneering civic leader, she is the Founder and Trustee of Women Empowerment Network UK and serves as Trustee of UKTA, advocating for public engagement, social justice, and representation for the Telugu and wider diaspora.

name: Gursharan Sian
org: FY Knitting & Crocheting / Let’s Go Southall
summary: Gursharan Sian leads the FY Knitting & Crocheting Group under the Let’s Go Southall Campaign, uniting community members through craft and companionship. Her group handcrafts warm clothing and essentials for homeless shelters, premature infants, hospices, and dementia facilities, alongside creating commemorative poppies for the Royal British Legion.
fullText:
I lead the FY Knitting & Crocheting Group, part of the Let’s Go Southall Campaign. I am passionate about teaching people how to knit and crochet, helping members develop new skills while building friendships and community connections.
Under my guidance, the group creates handmade knitted and crocheted items that are donated to those in need, including homeless people, premature babies, care home residents, the Salvation Army, Ealing Hospice, and Dementia Concern. The group also responds to requests from charities, producing much-needed items such as hats, blankets, and other handmade essentials.
In addition, our group has lovingly created and donated handmade poppies to the Royal British Legion in Greenford, supporting remembrance activities and honouring those who have served.

As Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh UK lead for Parliament Week, she drives youth civic engagement, earning volunteer awards from both Houses of Parliament. She also serves as Chair of Political Engagement at the Hindu Forum of Britain and Trustee of Param Shakti Peeth UK.
fullText:
• PhD Neuroscience with the Medical Research Council UK. Thesis: Properties of Olfactory Stem Cells for the Repair of Spinal Cord Injuries.
• I live in the UK with my family.
• A passionate advocate for social and community work and I have an outstanding record of public service – both to the British Indian diaspora and the wider community.

name: Hema Manjunath
org: Rangoli Radio / Indian Choir of England
summary: Hema Manjunath has contributed over 15 years of voluntary cultural service in Chester. A vocalist with The Indian Choir of England and certified Hindu Chaplain, she has produced over 240 episodes of her show 'Memories and Melodies' on Rangoli Radio, co-hosted 150 broadcasts, and serves Manchester Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan.
fullText: Hema Manjunath in Chester has been a Volunteer for more than 15 years in various Indian & Asian Cultural, Musical, Charity & Spiritual Events in the UK. For over 10 years, Hema is a Singer in The Indian Choir of England, also an Interfaith Speaker representing Hinduism, a Bhajan Singer & Event Co-Organiser. Since more than 5 years, she has been a prominent Volunteer Presenter in Rangoli Radio, a Community initiative & has produced 240 episodes of her own Show titled Memories and Melodies, also co-hosted over 150 Shows. Hema Manjunath is an Anchor at various events. Since 2 years, she has been a Management Committee Member in Manchester Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan. Hema has certified as a Hindu Chaplin this year.

name: Hema Yellapragada
org: Hindu Education Board UK / Women Stepping Out
summary: Hema Yellapragada serves as a Trustee of the Hindu Education Board UK and Women Stepping Out. Through the education board, she equips UK educators with authoritative curriculum resources for Religious Education, fostering authentic understanding of Hindu philosophy and traditions. With Women Stepping Out, she helps lead a multicultural peer-support charity providing vital mental health and crisis assistance to women.
fullText:
I am a trustee of Hindu Education Board UK since its inception. The Hindu Education Board UK (HEB UK) is a registered charity (Charity Number: 1199641) dedicated to improving the teaching and understanding of Hindu Dharma (Hinduism) across the UK education system. The primary objective of the board is to equip educators with authentic resources to confidently teach Hindu theology, philosophy, and traditions.
Support for Teachers: It provides lesson plans, training, and consultancy to teachers, exam boards, and educational publishers.
Student Focus: It aims to build a deep cultural and philosophical literacy for students aged 4 to 14, helping them develop a global perspective.
Parental Awareness: It works to raise awareness among Hindu parents regarding the importance of Religious Education (RE).
Here is our website https://www.hindueducationboarduk.org/

name: Himavalli Chalikonda
org: Telugu People in UK (TPUK) / Telugu Naari UK
summary: Himavalli Chalikonda has led Telugu People in UK and Telugu Naari UK since 2008, organizing extensive disaster relief, medical scholarships, and youth school supplies. She coordinates the British Telugu Community Forum under Lord Uday Nagaraju to foster civic participation, and established the FACE of Naari Awards celebrating female social leaders.
fullText:
Celebrating Community Service, Cultural Heritage and Women’s Empowerment
Himavalli Chalikonda has been dedicated to community service since 2006, working tirelessly to support people in need, preserve Telugu language and culture, and uplift women and families across the UK and beyond. Since 2008, she has led two vibrant community initiatives, Telugu People in UK (TPUK) and Telugu Naari UK, providing platforms for mutual support, cultural connection, community information and women’s empowerment.
Her charitable work over the years has supported communities affected by natural disasters, vulnerable families, students and children in need. Her initiatives include fundraising for victims of the Andhra Pradesh floods in 2009 and 2014, the Haiti earthquake in 2010, and the Uttarakhand floods in 2013. In 2015, she supported people affected by the Chennai floods by arranging essential supplies and donating to Aide et Action. In 2020, she helped raise funds through Memu Saitham to provide grocery kits for 108 families affected by the Rayalaseema floods. In 2022, she supported a medical student with college fees, raised funds for 40 Adivasi families who lost their belongings in a fire in Warangal, and helped a talented athlete with competition expenses. Since 2022, she has also supported a world champion athlete with gym expenses. In 2024, she helped raise funds to provide schoolbags, books, pencil boxes and sports kits to orphaned children studying in government schools in Telangana.. Her wider charitable efforts have included fundraising for children battling cancer, supporting girls experiencing period poverty, and assisting families of students who tragically lost their lives while studying in the UK between 2008 and 2014.
Himavalli has consistently championed women’s empowerment, organising career-development and skills sessions, promoting autism awareness, addressing domestic violence, and raising awareness of foster care and adoption. In 2022, she introduced the FACE of Naari Awards to recognise women leaders who demonstrate social responsibility. Her dedication to preserving Telugu culture has also included organising cultural events, showcasing local talent and creating opportunities for the Telugu diaspora to remain connected to its heritage.
Her community involvement extends to civic participation and representation. Himavalli has volunteered in British Indian election campaigns through both in-person participation and online campaigning. She also voluntarily coordinated a meeting initiated by Lord Uday Nagaraju of Bloomsbury, bringing together councillors, political candidates, community leaders and young people from across the political spectrum to strengthen British Telugu representation in public life. Under Lord Uday’s leadership and vision, the British Telugu Community Forum (BTCF) aims to build a politically neutral network that mentors future leaders, encourages civic participation and serves communities across the UK.
Himavalli has also been nominated twice as APNRT UK Country Coordinator by the Government of Andhra Pradesh to promote APNRT services among the Telugu diaspora. Her longstanding commitment to service reflects the values of compassion, inclusion and cultural pride. Through years of voluntary work, fundraising, community leadership and advocacy, she continues to inspire others to support those in need and contribute towards a stronger, more connected society.

name: Janki Desai
summary: Janki Desai is the founder of the Bradford Girls Group, creating an inclusive community initiative where families and women connect through traditional Garba, Bollywood fitness, arts, and cultural excursions. Over more than six years of voluntary service, she has also helped organize the Bradford Diwali Lights Opening Ceremony, reducing social isolation and building strong community solidarity.
fullText:
For over six years, I have been committed to making a positive impact by bringing people together through cultural, social, and wellbeing initiatives. I believe that strong communities are built by creating opportunities where people feel connected, supported, and inspired to grow.
As the founder of the Bradford Girls Group for more than five years, I have created an inclusive space where women and families can build friendships, improve their wellbeing, and celebrate Indian culture. I regularly organise Garba workshops, Rangoli workshops, arts and crafts activities, Bollywood fitness sessions, community trips, competitions, and cultural events that encourage people of all ages to participate, learn new skills, and build lasting friendships.
Over the years, I have worked closely with many Hindu communities, voluntary organisations, and local community groups to organise and support a wide range of cultural and community events. My focus has always been on preserving traditions, promoting cultural awareness, encouraging inclusion, and bringing people from different backgrounds together through shared experiences.
Volunteering is at the heart of everything I do. My aim is to empower people, especially women and families, to feel confident, valued, and connected. By creating opportunities to learn, celebrate, and support one another, I hope to continue building stronger, more inclusive communities where everyone feels they belong and where culture becomes a bridge that unites people.

name: Jayeeta Ghosh
summary: Jayeeta Ghosh is an accomplished British-Indian classical vocalist and Founder-Director of the Geetanjali Academy of Fine Arts. She integrates Hindustani classical music with community wellbeing, pioneering innovative music therapy programmes for autistic and non-verbal children, teenagers facing anxiety, and senior care residents across Northwest London.
fullText: Jayeeta Ghosh is a prominent British-Indian vocalist, music educator, and entrepreneur based in Northwest London. She is most widely known as the Founder and Director of the Geetanjali Academy of Fine Arts (GAOFAL), a leading institution dedicated to Hindustani classical music. Her work bridges classical Indian traditions with community-focused well-being, specifically pioneering music-based therapies for children with special needs and autism

name: Kalavathi Thirunavukkarasu
org: British Indian Nurses Association / Tamil Arvalar
summary: Kalavathi Thirunavukkarasu is an Advanced Clinical Practitioner based in Derby and an executive lead for the British Indian Nurses Association. For over six years, she has mentored newly arrived healthcare professionals navigating NHS career progression. She also co-founded the Tamil Arvalar group eight years ago to preserve Tamil language and cultural traditions for the younger generation.
fullText:
I am an Advanced Clinical Practitioner work in Derby> I am from Tamil community. I and my friends have started Tamil Arvalar group 8 years ago, in order to support our Tamil community and younger generation for maintaining our Tamil culture in the UK.
I am a volunteer executives lead for British Indian Nurses Association for last 6 years supporting new nurses to progress in their careers.

name: Kalpana Doshi
org: Laughter Yoga / Victoria and Albert Museum
summary: Kalpana Doshi is a certified Laughter Yoga practitioner and Visitor Experience Assistant at the Victoria and Albert Museum. For over twelve years, she has utilized mindfulness, joy, and laughter therapy across festivals, care homes, and wellness retreats to reduce anxiety and build connection. At the V&A, she delivers public presentations on South Asian art, including the historic 1851 ivory Durga shrine.
fullText: Kalpana Doshi is a Certified Laughter Yoga practitioner based in Central London. She is a leading wellness advocate, community builder and healthy living mentor. Since training with Doctor Kataria School of Laughter Yoga in 2012, she has shared laughter, mindfulness and human connection with people from all walks of life. She has led laughter sessions at festivals, corporate organisations, charities, care homes and community groups. Her work has featured for several years at Diwali in Trafalgar Square, Camp Bestival and international well being retreats. Kalpana believes laughter can reduce stress, lift our spirits and bring people together. Her inspiring journey is featured in the book "Voices from Gujarat" celebrating influential British Gujarati women. Kalpana also works at the Victoria & Albert museum in South Kensington. Through her Visitor Experience role, she gives regular talks on the remarkable ivory shrine of Goddess Durga which was in the Indian Pavilion at The Great Exhibition of 1851. Whether sharing Indian art and heritage or leading Laughter Yoga, Kalpana is on a mission to bring more laughter into people's lives, spread joy, create meaningful connections and leave a little sparkle wherever she goes.

name: Kamna Saini
summary: Kamna Saini is an entrepreneur, educator, and cultural advocate based in Pinner, holding a Master’s in Sanskrit and qualifications in education and naturopathy. As the founder of ventures including Venturis Holding, Nexdyn.ai, and Kams Couture, alongside the community initiative Sanskruti, she actively promotes Indian heritage, traditions, and festivals across the UK, creating vibrant spaces for cultural connection, intergenerational learning, and community unity.
fullText:
My name is Kamna Saini, and I am proud to call Pinner my home. Originally from Rajasthan, India, I grew up in a close-knit joint family where I learned the importance of respect, compassion, togetherness, and staying connected to my roots. These values have shaped the person I am today and continue to guide me in both my personal and professional life.
Education has always been an important part of my journey. I hold a Master’s degree in Sanskrit, a Diploma in Naturopathy, and a Bachelor of Education. My diverse educational background reflects my curiosity, my love for learning, and my belief that knowledge opens doors to new possibilities.
Over the years, my journey has evolved into entrepreneurship, where I have had the opportunity to turn my ideas and ambitions into reality. I am the founder of three businesses: Venturis Holding, Nexdyn.ai, and Kams Couture. Each venture represents a different aspect of my interests, creativity, and vision, and building these businesses has been a journey of learning, courage, and personal growth.
While I am passionate about my professional aspirations, my family remains at the heart of everything I do. I am a proud wife to Satish Saini and a proud mother to my talented daughter, who inspires me every day. Balancing family and business has taught me resilience, patience, and the importance of believing in myself, even when the journey is challenging.
For me, success is not just about qualifications, business ventures, or achievements. It is about staying grounded in my values, having the courage to explore new opportunities, embracing change, and inspiring others through my journey. I believe that our roots give us strength, while our dreams encourage us to grow beyond our comfort zones.
As I continue my journey, I hope to make a meaningful contribution through my work, represent my cultural heritage with pride, and encourage other women to believe in their abilities and pursue their ambitions with confidence.

name: Kirti Soni
org: Jeevan Organ & Blood Donation / Grenfell Responder
summary: Kirti Soni is a psychotherapist and founder of Jeevan Organ and Blood Donation, partnering with the NHS to address donor shortages among ethnic minority communities. A first responder supporting Grenfell survivors, she established 24/7 mental health helplines during COVID-19 and serves on the Parajiya Pattni Association committee.
fullText: You could say Kirti Soni's empathy and welfare for others dates right back to her arrival in UK, when although she was a child under 10 herself, when she saw the ads by NSPCC and other charities she started doing all sorts of sponsored activities to help the plight of others. Then, when her hopes of going to 6th form and then University were cut short by marriage, she made it her mission to support all other youngsters to achieve their dreams and to raise parental awareness about this and about integration across all ethnicities . Her marital life took her to living in the Middle East and India where again she did the same plus providing mental health support for many British, US and European expat communities there. In return to UK she served as a psychotherapist for troubled teens and at Universities. And after a personal loss she turned her anger into action as Founder of Jeevan Organ and Blood Donation working with the NHS as a sewa to raise awareness amongst all the ethnic minorities because that's where the donor shortage was greatest. She was also part of the First Responders at Grenfell and continues to support the community there. In addition she cited the advance of a mysterious "flu" to the UK government as early as January 2020, before it was declared by World Health Organisation in March 2020. This led to her as Founder Covid19 Mental Health Support where she led a team providing 24/7 support to people locally and internationally, which is still running to date. Alongside the above she has assisted IIW, IIL , Hindu Council and Cancer Support is just a few examples, as well as her own community Parajiya Pattni Association where she has been on the Executive Committee for 4years, but a serving member since it was formed 50years ago.

name: Malathy Muthu
summary: Malathy Muthu is the Founder and CEO of Skills Enterprise, a Newham-based charity supporting approximately 1,700 vulnerable residents annually through digital literacy, employment pathways, and women's economic independence. Recognized with a Newham Changemaker Award and praised in Parliament, she advises national panels on essential digital skills and co-leads the Women in Newham Network.
fullText:
SELF-BIO DECLARATION
Name: Mrs Malathy Muthu ( Mala)
Role: Founder, CEO- Skills Enterprise (Charity No. 1120254)
I was born and raised in Tamil Nadu, South India, before moving to the United Kingdom as an adult. Like many migrants, I found myself navigating an unfamiliar system - unfamiliar processes for welfare, work and belonging - largely on my own. That experience of disorientation, and of the quiet relief that comes when someone finally helps you find your way, became the foundation of everything I have built since.
Nearly twenty years ago, I founded Skills Enterprise, a community charity based in Manor Park, in the London Borough of Newham - one of the most diverse and, by several national measures, most deprived boroughs in England. What began as a response to my own lived experience has grown into an organisation that now supports approximately 1,700 residents every year through digital inclusion, welfare and benefits navigation, employment support, and programmes dedicated to women's economic empowerment.
As Founder, CEO and Projects Manager, I have carried responsibility for every dimension of the organisation - fundraising, governance, HR, legal compliance and frontline delivery - often simultaneously.
In 2025, one of our participants, Kalpana, was cited by the Minister for Data Protection and Telecoms, Sir Chris Bryant, at London Tech Week - a moment that reflected years of quiet, unglamorous work finally being seen on a national stage.
My work has also been recognised at the highest levels of public life. Skills Enterprise has hosted a visit from the House of Lords Communications and Digital Committee, and I was invited to speak directly about the lived experience of poverty and migration that shapes our approach. We have welcomed Baroness Hilary Armstrong and representatives of the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology to our centre, and I currently sit on the DSIT Essential Digital Skills Framework refresh panel, contributing the perspective of a frontline, migrant-led community organisation to national policy.
Skills Enterprise was named UK Online Centre of the Year in 2023/24 and was a finalist for the ISPA Award in 2025. I was recognised with a Newham Changemaker Award, and in a speech to Parliament, the Rt Hon Stephen Timms MP praised our rapid pivot during the COVID-19 pandemic, when we distributed devices to digitally excluded residents, scaled our support by 50%, and guided people through Universal Credit applications, online banking and job searches - helping many households save over £300 a year on energy costs in the process.
Women's empowerment sits at the heart of my personal mission, not only as a programme strand but as a lived commitment.
I co-lead the Women in Newham Network (WiNN) alongside Newham Community Partnership, and I continue to develop new initiatives - including a physical activity and wellbeing programme for local women and a multilingual digital and civic literacy platform - designed specifically to reach women who are otherwise isolated by language, confidence or circumstance. Many of the women who walk through our doors arrive the way I once did: uncertain, underestimated, and simply looking for someone to show them the way. Helping them find their footing, and in many cases go on to work, training or independence, remains the most meaningful part of my life's work.
Beyond the organisation I lead, I remain rooted in the Tamil community in the UK, and I have been honoured for community service at a Tamil business event in recognition of this work.
It would be a profound honour to be recognised through the Inspiring Indian Women Award, not for myself alone, but on behalf of the many South Asian women I have had the privilege of walking alongside over the past two decades - women whose courage and resilience inspire me as much as, I hope, we have been able to support them.

name: Manjiri Gokhale Joshi
summary: Manjiri Gokhale Joshi is the co-founder of Maya CARE Foundation, coordinating over 2,000 volunteers across 72 Indian cities, 4 UK cities, and Nepal to assist elderly citizens, managed entirely by persons with disabilities. A former CEO and Oxford Said Business School EDI head, she is pursuing doctoral research on inclusion.
fullText: Manjiri is co-founder of Maya CARE Foundation providing free assistance to the elderly in 72 Indian cities, 4 UK cities and Nepal through a network of 2000 plus volunteers and managed by a team of professionals on wheelchairs/visual impairment. She was one of 12 professionals among 13,000 applicants selected by LinkedIn to assist Virgin Founder Sir Richard Branson to select, judge and mentor entreprenurs pitching for a £1million fund.

name: Manpreet Maycock
org: British Army Reserve / Women's Mentoring & Commonwealth Heritage
summary: LCpl Manpreet Maycock is a British Army Reservist and dedicated mentor committed to empowering women and young girls. Drawing from her personal journey, she conducts school visits, mentoring sessions, and inspirational talks to help women overcome adversity and build self-reliance. She also actively champions Commonwealth remembrance through her work supporting the Commonwealth Gates Memorial initiative.
fullText: LCpl Manpreet Maycock is a British Army Reservist and mother whose experiences have shaped her commitment to encouraging women and girls. Through mentoring, school visits and public speaking, she shares her journey to help women, particularly those facing difficult circumstances or balancing family responsibilities, build confidence and see new possibilities. She wants them to know that hardship need not define their future and that women can rebuild, serve, lead and support one another. She has also contributed to the Commonwealth Gates Memorial initiative, helping ensure that the service and sacrifice of Commonwealth personnel, including women who served during the two World Wars, are remembered.

name: Mayuri Patel
org: Ipswich Gujarati School / Interfaith & Community Leadership
summary: Mayuri Patel has dedicated over 25 years to voluntary service, cultural preservation, and interfaith dialogue. As Chair of Ipswich Gujarati School and Trustee of multiple faith forums, she promotes language education and cultural integration across Suffolk. Her leadership in organizing major festivals and coordinating mobile vaccination clinics during the pandemic earned her the HFMA Eastern Champion of Diversity Award.
fullText: Mayuri Patel has dedicated more than 25 years to community service, cultural education, and promoting inclusion. She is Chair of Ipswich Gujarati School since 2001, Trustee of The Interfaith and Spirituality Network Suffolk and The Ipswich Faith and Community Forum and previously served as Vice Chair of Ipswich Hindu Samaj 2006-2023. She also served as Treasurer and a committee member of the Ipswich and Suffolk Indian Association for over a decade, helping to organise major annual events including Holi, Diwali, and Ipswich Mela, celebrating Indian culture and bringing together people from diverse backgrounds. For the past four years, she has actively supported South Asian Heritage Month celebrations, promoting greater understanding and appreciation of South Asian heritage within the wider community. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she played a key role in organising community vaccination clinics and coordinating visits from the mobile vaccination bus, helping to improve vaccine access and uptake within local communities.

name: Revd Paditayin Meeta Joshi
org: University of Surrey Hindu Chaplaincy / Community Leadership
summary: Revd Paditayin Meeta Joshi has served for a decade heading the Hindu Chaplaincy at the University of Surrey, supporting over 1,800 students and staff. A Surrey Minority Ethnic Forum Ambassador and Deputy Chair of Woking People of Faith, she established Surrey's first interfaith sporting events, represented grassroots communities at the UN Commission on the Status of Women, and built Guildford's first permanent Hindu shrine.
fullText:
Meeta Joshi is a multi-hyphenated community icon, with a professional and philanthropic portfolio spanning IT, Media, multi-faith and higher education.
For 10 years she has headed the Hindu Chaplaincy at the University of Surrey, now serving as Revd. Ptd. to over 1.8k Hindu students and staff. She has pioneered transformative community-building initatives in her local area and beyond, as a Surrey Minority Ethnic Forum Ambassador, Deputy Chair of Woking People of Faith, and more. She organised Surrey's first ever Interfaith cricket and football events, which have become community staples. She also served as Project Manager,for the Mayor of Guildford's first ever Multicultural Diversity Show, Meeta enriche the lives of people in her community for over a decade through her honorary work as a Chaplain and Hindu community leader, setting example for building bridges across faiths for social good. She has spoken at high level forums including the UN Commission on the Status of Women, helping shedlight on grassroots and underrepresented communities, and serves as Non- Executive Director for the Justina Mutale Leadership Foundation, and MC at NAWO. She builds a home away from home for thousands of international newcomers to her local community , setting up Guildford's first ever permemant Hindu shrine at the University of Surrey.

name: Neelam Chawla
summary: Neelam Chawla is the Founder and Director of Maxable Global CIC, a community organization committed to proactive mental health awareness, resilience, and social inclusion. Holding an MSc in Psychology of Mental Health and Wellbeing, she created the Maxable Resilience Framework and leads multi-generational programmes including youth initiatives, men's forums, and seniors' wellness circles that remove barriers to emotional support.
fullText:
Neelam Chawla
Founder & Director, Maxable® Global
A recipient of multiple national and international awards for her contributions to mental health awareness and community engagement, Neelam Chawla is a mental health and resilience advocate. She brings an extensive background in education, inclusive education and community development, alongside an MSc in Psychology of Mental Health and Wellbeing.
Through her not-for-profit community organisation, Maxable Global CIC, she champions mental wellbeing and prevention, guided by the belief that support should begin long before difficulties escalate.
Her charitable work reaches across generations, engaging children, young people, men, women and older adults through awareness campaigns, resilience workshops, creative activities and community programmes. Many of these initiatives are offered free of charge, helping remove financial barriers and making participation accessible to people from diverse backgrounds.
Recognising that stigma, isolation and cultural expectations can discourage people from speaking openly or seeking support, she creates welcoming spaces where conversations begin, friendships develop and individuals feel heard, valued and included.
She has also developed the Maxable Resilience Framework (M-RF), a practical approach to strengthening emotional resilience, encouraging reflection and fostering meaningful human connections.
Among her recognitions is the honour of Ambassador of Peace, conferred by a human rights organisation in India.
At the heart of her work is a simple belief: meaningful connections are essential to better mental health and stronger communities.

name: Neelima Penumarthy
summary: Neelima Penumarthy, an Imperial College Chevening Scholar, founded StoryHour in 2016 to bridge cultural divides through accessible storytelling. She engages intergenerational teams—youth and elderly narrators—to produce audiobooks and puppet shows based on Indian epics, collaborating with institutes for the visually impaired and earning BBC recognition for her educational productions.
fullText:
I am a producer whose motto is to "Connect Cultures" through stories. I started "StoryHour" in 2016 with our debut audiobook, "Ramayana : An Ancient Indian Epic", written and narrated by two teenage brothers. My aim through StoryHour is to convey stories in an hour, in audiobook format. I work with teenagers and the elderly community as my writers and narrators to convey stories from India, as audiobooks as well as puppet shows. I moved to London in 1996 on the prestigious British Chevening scholarship to pursue M.Sc in Chemistry at Imperial College, London. I have raised two sons in the UK, through whom my journey into the world of storytelling began, with the retelling of the Ramayana as an audiobook. They became my first teenage writers and narrators. The audiobook went on to receive accolades. I worked with three students from Devnar Insitute for the Blind, Hyderabad for the Telugu version of our Ramayana audiobook. My next audiobook is on the Indian Independence, written and narrated by two teenagers, in English. For the Hindi version of the audiobook, I worked with two students from Blind Relief Association, Delhi as my Hindi narrators. During Covid, I engaged the elderly community in my family by asking them to write short stories for children that convey the meaning of Telugu proverbs, called Samethalu. I along with some of my Telugu friends narrated these stories. A month ago, I added animations to the stories to make them more illustrative.
I worked with artists from London to produce a puppet show on the Ramayana, which has been featured on the BBC in 2019, 2024.
Through my work, I want to continue to work with young , raw talent and empower them to develop their language skills, both written and spoken. I believe in the power of language, expression and art of story telling. India is a land of stories and I am striving to share those stories with the world in multiple languages.

name: Nina Darmeci

summary: Nina Darmeci is a dedicated community volunteer who provides complimentary dance classes for special educational needs (SEN) schoolchildren and parents.
