fullText: Nina Darmeci is heavily involved with community service such offering free dance service to SEN ( special educational needs school children and parents ) , offering Zumba to British heart foundation to help build strong heart, donations to various organisation as part of IIW , offering free dance session to elderly community , and care homes.

name: Nithya Sowmy
summary: Nithya Sowmy teaches traditional devotional music, chants, and Lalitha Sahasranamam, connecting women and children to their spiritual heritage. She volunteers actively for temple events and leverages her social media platforms to promote women entrepreneurs, fostering community connection and economic growth.
fullText: I am passionate about preserving and promoting our rich Hindu culture, traditions, and Sanatana Dharma, especially among the younger generation living abroad. Through my music and sloka classes, I teach children and adults the beauty of devotional music, sacred chants, and our spiritual heritage, helping them stay connected to their roots while living in a foreign land. I have also taught the powerful Lalitha Sahasranamam to numerous women, making them to enter the Lalitha Sadhana which empowers them to embrace spirituality and incorporate its positive influence into their everyday lives. Beyond my cultural and spiritual initiatives, I actively support women entrepreneurs by helping promote their businesses, products, and services, enabling them to reach wider audiences through my social media channels. I also dedicate my time to volunteering for temple activities and supporting temple initiatives through promotions and community engagement. Through all these efforts, my aim is to bring people together, empower women, preserve our timeless traditions, and pass on the invaluable wisdom of Sanatana Dharma to future generations.

name: Niyta Radia
org: London Air Ambulance / Single Mothers Mentorship
summary: Niyta Radia is an entrepreneur and community fundraiser who overcame life-threatening physical trauma and medical adversity to inspire others. She actively mentors single mothers navigating hardship and spearheads prominent fundraising initiatives for the London Air Ambulance, while contributing her voluntary time to cultural and charitable celebrations across London.
fullText:
I’m now 63 years old , I became a single Mum of 2 boys , 30 years ago . Life was a real struggle .juggling young children ,work, and no money ! . At the same time up lifting , encouraging and motivating other single mothers . Determination , inner strength and positivity kept me going . I changed careers from travel to property . In 2006 I set up my own estate agency & started developing properties .
In 2009, suddenly my Father died which really hit me hard . Then 2010 I had a building site accident where I fell 20 feet . London Air Ambulance saved my life and took me to Royal London hospital . I had fractures in my spine and pelvis with incidental clots in my lungs - i learnt to walk again .After that was mis-diagnosed with Lymphoma . I knew I couldn’t give up as now my widowed Mum and my children needed me . I fought the battles and carried on , as being the only bread winner. In 2019 , I was on life support and a coma with 11.5cm clot in the aorta, it caused brain damage, memory loss , it left me with a heart condition and a clotting disorder - again I was lucky and survived against all odds.. I have been on my death bed four times with brain bleeds too . Now I raise funds for London Air Ambulance when I can , . I live each day as my last , with empathy & kindness and inspire others to live life to the full and to have inner strength and never to give up no matter what . , I organise days out and try to impire and support women that need guidance.

name: Padmini Vijayaraghavan
summary: Padmini Vijayaraghavan is an enterprise cybersecurity architect and traditional Parai arts advocate. She founded Dance Dreamers to empower women through dance, while co-leading London Parai and London Sangamam to preserve folk Tamil arts, alongside exploring AI technology solutions through her venture AinthinAI.
fullText:
I'm a Cybersecurity Architect by profession, a Parai artist by passion, a dancer at heart, an entrepreneur by ambition, and a community builder by choice.
With over 15 years in technology, I've built my career around solving complex challenges, leading teams and creating meaningful change.
But my identity goes far beyond my profession.
As the founder of Dance Dreamers, I've worked to create a space where women can rediscover their confidence, celebrate themselves and grow together.
My passion for Tamil traditional arts has taken me on a journey of breaking stereotypes, challenging social barriers and helping preserve our cultural heritage. Through London Parai and London Sangamam, I believe in giving our traditional artists the recognition, respect and stage they deserve.
As the founder of AinthinAI, I'm also exploring how technology and innovation can empower businesses and communities.
I believe in creating opportunities rather than waiting for them, challenging limitations rather than accepting them, and building something meaningful that lasts beyond me.
I'm not defined by one role. I'm a woman who believes in building her own path and making space for others along the way.

name: Paromita Goswani
summary: Paromita Goswani is the founder of Jaltarang, a social enterprise dedicated to supporting acid attack survivors, promoting girl child education, and championing autism awareness. An internationally acclaimed filmmaker, she produces and directs impactful films addressing critical social issues such as child hunger and infant mortality, leveraging storytelling to drive lasting community change.
fullText:
Founder of Jaltarang
Paromita Goswani has been a passionate advocate for social causes, championing autism awareness, supporting acid attack survivors through her social enterprise, Jaltarang, and promoting girl child education. Through her work as a filmmaker, she has also produced and directed films that raise awareness about critical social issues, including child hunger, earning international acclaim for her efforts. name: Prafula Shah
org: Oshwal Association of the UK / Organ Donation Alliance
summary: Prafula Shah is the first woman elected President in the 55-year history of the Oshwal Association of the UK. A living kidney donor and NHS Blood and Transplant Ambassador, she chairs the Jain and Hindu Organ Donation Alliance to raise life-saving awareness. Her 40 years of service also include founding Thriving Tuesdays for elder care and leading community devotional circles.
fullText:
​For over 40 years, I have been privileged to serve communities across the UK through faith, health, wellbeing and voluntary leadership. My guiding principle has always been simple: to use my time, skills and experience in selfless service (sewa) to help others and strengthen our communities. In May 2026, I was deeply honoured to become the first woman elected President of the Oshwal Association of the UK in its 55-year history. Leading one of the UK's largest Jain organisations is both a privilege and a responsibility, as we work to create a community where everyone can connect, belong and inspire.
As Chair of the Jain and Hindu Organ Donation Alliance, a living kidney donor and an NHS Blood and Transplant Ambassador, I am passionate about raising awareness of organ donation, challenging cultural misconceptions and encouraging life-saving conversations within South Asian communities.
My commitment to community also includes chairing Bhakti Mandal, a weekly devotional group that brings together around 80 people every Friday for bhajans and pooja, and founding Thriving Tuesdays, a grant-funded wellbeing programme supporting older people in Harrow through gentle exercise, music and friendship. Reducing isolation, encouraging friendships and health literacy.
I believe leadership is about bringing people together, empowering others and leaving every community stronger than you found it. If my journey inspires even one person​ - especially another woman​ - to step forward and serve, then I will consider my greatest achievement to be not what I have accomplished, but the opportunities I have helped create for others.

name: Dr Priya Virmani
org: Paint Our World / Vedic Philosophy & Wellbeing
summary: Dr Priya Virmani is a Bristol University PhD graduate, author, TEDx orator, and founder of the children’s charity Paint Our World, supporting disadvantaged youth into higher education. For two decades, she has communicated Vedic philosophy, emotional intelligence, and mindfulness, presenting widely across temples, public institutions, and the UK Parliament to foster compassionate living.
fullText:
Dr Priya Virmani is a wellness consultant, spiritual counsellor, author, orator and TEDx speaker, with a lifelong passion for understanding how ancient Indian wisdom (the Mahabharata, the Gita, the Ramayana, Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, Yoga, Ayurveda, Vastu Shastri etc) can enrich modern life.
She holds a PhD from the University of Bristol and has written for more than 100 publications including in the UK, India, China, Hong Kong, Middle East, the USA etc. Her evidenced journey in service and education began in childhood and in her twenties, she founded a children’s charity, Paint Our World, which continues to thrive today supporting underprivileged children who have now progressed to university.
Over the past two decades, she has devoted herself to researching and communicating Vedic philosophy, psychology, emotional intelligence and wellbeing in ways that are relevant and accessible to contemporary audiences. Her work has taken her into temples, organisations and public forums in the U.K. and internationally, where she speaks and teaches on wellbeing, resilience, emotional intelligence, spirituality and the wisdom traditions of India.
She is particularly passionate about creating bridges between cultures and generations — preserving the depth of India’s ancient knowledge while making it meaningful for modern Britain and the wider world. At the heart of her work is a simple belief: wisdom becomes truly valuable when it is shared in a way that helps people live with greater awareness, compassion and purpose.

name: Puja Lakhmania
summary: Puja Lakhmania is a community activist and founder of Events2Empower based in Barking and Dagenham, dedicated to uplifting women and families. She leads initiatives providing domestic abuse awareness, volunteer mentoring, and health wellbeing workshops. Collaborating closely with local councils, libraries, and public health teams, she delivers inclusive cultural festivals, hot meals, and family health events.
fullText: I am Puja Lakhmania, a social activist, community organiser and mother of two based in Barking and Dagenham. I am passionate about empowering women, supporting families and bringing communities together. My charitable work includes women’s empowerment projects, helping volunteers build confidence and skills, and creating a platform to raise awareness of domestic violence so women feel heard and supported. I organise cultural celebrations, children’s activities, women’s fitness and health awareness events, alongside helping provide free or affordable activities and hot meals. My community work involves Barking Library, the local council, Vaccination UK and public health teams, including a successful MMR family fun day. Proud of my Indian heritage, I strive to create welcoming spaces where everyone feels valued, included and connected.

name: Purnima Raval
summary: Purnima Raval is a trailblazing retired police officer who served 35 years in the Metropolitan Police Service, becoming the first Asian policewoman to receive the Police Long Service and Good Conduct Medal. A champion of equality and safeguarding, she continues to mentor young women and spotlight unsung community heroes.
fullText:
I am a pioneer Asian policewoman , trailblazer , change maker and an advocate for equality , inclusivity and diversity.
I served as a frontline operational police officer in The Metropolitan Police Service for 35 years , the first Asian policewoman in the UK recipient of the Police Long Service and Good Conduct medal.
It was a privilege and honour to serve and am immensely proud of my contribution , achievements and success shaping Policing , safeguarding communities from harm , community cohesion , investigating crimes bringing justice , solace for victims / families of horrific crimes and their perpetrators to justice.
Raised in a loving Hindu family passionate about the rich Heritage of India , its culture and values of strong sense of duty , hard work , respect , selfless service to humanity following the path of truth , justice and righteousness.
The empowerment of youth and women are very close to my heart .
Throughout my career and post retirement aspire and inspire by mentoring , coaching , supporting making their dreams a reality. Also raising awareness and shining a light on the BAME Unsung Heroes past and present.
Received many awards , commendations for my work with the communities , investigations both from the police , judiciary and outside organisations.
Proud to be associated with Team IIW , well done all for the excellent work.
Congratulations on our 10th anniversary !

name: Raga D'silva
summary: Raga D'silva is an author, film producer, and prominent advocate for LGBTQ+ rights. Through her platform Older Queer Voices, she connects generations, conducting research, podcasts, and literary productions to ensure older queer stories and lived experiences are preserved with dignity, inclusion, and visibility.
fullText: Over the years, I have dedicated my voice and creative work to the LGBT+ community, continuing despite the challenges and prejudice that remain. Through Older Queer Voices, I bring generations together and make older LGBT+ people’s lives and experiences visible through research, our podcast, events, writing books and films. This work challenges assumptions, preserves stories that might otherwise go unheard, and builds understanding across generations. I believe everyone deserves to live with dignity, to be heard and to know they belong.

name: Ragasudha Vinjamuri
org: Sanskruti Centre for Cultural Excellence / University of Sunderland in London
summary: Ragasudha Vinjamuri is an Associate Lecturer in the Faculty of Business and Law at the University of Sunderland in London. She founded the Sanskruti Centre for Cultural Excellence, a registered arts charity. name: Reena Bagga
org: Mental Health Advocacy & PND Support / Wellbeing & Personal Empowerment
summary: Reena Bagga is a dedicated mental health advocate, postnatal depression (PND) specialist, domestic violence ambassador, podcast host, and social media strategist. Over a nine-year journey of personal transformation and rediscovery, she has championed emotional wellbeing, rebuilt confidence, and empowered women to rediscover their voice, embrace their aspirations, and realize their full potential.
fullText:
Mental Health Advocate | PND Specialist | Wellbeing & DV Ambassador | Social Media Entrepreneur & Business Strategist | Podcast Host
For nine years, Reena has been on a journey of rediscovering herself. It has meant rebuilding confidence, finding her voice and recognising the importance of her own aspirations alongside the responsibilities she carries. Her story is not about becoming someone entirely new. It is about reconnecting with the woman she always had the potential to be.

name: Reena Ranger OBE
summary: Reena Ranger OBE co-founded Women Empowered in 2012, creating an inspiring platform and charitable foundation that connects and mentors women across diverse backgrounds, for which she received an OBE. She has also served over ten years as an elected councillor for Three Rivers and Hertfordshire, and served as the first female Co-Chair of Conservative Friends of India.
fullText:
Reena Ranger OBE co-founded Women Empowered in 2012, creating a platform for women from all walks of life to come together, share their experiences and stories, support and mentor one another, and become more actively involved in their communities. Over the years, the initiative developed beyond its events to include a charitable arm and an online platform sharing stories, ideas and experiences to inspire and support others. Her sustained contribution through Women Empowered was recognised with the award of an OBE for services to BAME women.
Alongside this work, Reena has served as an elected councillor for Three Rivers since 2014, giving her more than a decade of direct experience representing residents and working with local communities on issues that affect their everyday lives. She also served as a Hertfordshire County Councillor from 2021 to 2025, with responsibilities including public health, community safety, highways and transport. As the first woman to serve as Co-Chair of Conservative Friends of India, she worked to encourage greater participation in public life, create opportunities for people to engage in politics and ensure that community voices were represented and heard. During her tenure, Conservative Friends of India grew to become the largest affiliated group.
Across these roles, her work has centred on connecting people, creating opportunities for participation and helping ensure that voices from different communities are heard.

name: Renu Gidoomal
summary: Renu Gidoomal is a London-based singer, songwriter and event host who sings in several languages, from bhajans to Bollywood and Sufi to soul. She leads Atmasphere Events Ltd and the fusion band Atmasphere, and has performed in more than 30 countries. She is a patron of Better Lives Foundation, a registered charity.
fullText: Renu Gidoomal is a London-based singer, songwriter and event host who sings in several languages, from bhajans to Bollywood and Sufi to soul. name: Ritu Saxena
summary: Ritu Saxena is an accomplished artist and community volunteer actively involved with IIW since 2020. She conducts Indian art and cultural workshops in schools, choreographs traditional Diwali dances, and coordinates charitable fundraising for temples, homeless relief, Cancer Research UK, and the Royal British Legion over 12 years of dedicated service.
fullText:
My Community Involvement, Voluntary Work and Charity Contributions
I have been actively involved with IIW since 2020, dedicating my time, skills, and efforts to supporting the community, promoting Indian culture, and empowering women.
Over the years, I have volunteered in schools, leading art activities for primary school children to introduce them to Indian culture, traditions, and Hindu festivals. I have also choreographed dances for Diwali celebrations, helping to preserve and share our rich cultural heritage with younger generations.
I have actively supported IIW events and initiatives, contributing wherever possible to empower women, encourage community participation, and make a positive difference in people’s lives.
I have also supported the Hindu Temple in Peterborough through donations and other efforts to help protect it from being taken over by the local council. I am currently actively involved in fundraising for Shri Kunj Bihari Temple in Harrow, UK. In addition, I have contributed towards providing food for homeless people and supporting those who are less fortunate.
As an artist, I have held art exhibitions at various venues across London and Buckinghamshire, using my creativity to engage with the wider community and promote artistic expression.
Charity and fundraising have always been close to my heart. I have actively participated in fundraising initiatives for Cancer Research UK, other cancer charities, and Diabetes UK, supporting important causes that affect many individuals and families.
Furthermore, I have supported the Royal British Legion for the past 12 years, demonstrating my continued commitment to honouring and supporting members of the Armed Forces community and veterans.
Alongside these activities, I have been actively involved with a local church, supporting its future programmes and charitable initiatives, including efforts to help an orphanage in Nepal and support other local community projects.
Through all these activities, I strive to contribute positively to society, promote cultural understanding, support charitable causes, and bring people together. I strongly believe that even small acts of kindness, when combined with the efforts of others, can make a meaningful and lasting difference in people’s lives.

name: Ritu Sharma
org: Kaushalya UK / Women's Empowerment & Mental Health
summary: Ritu Sharma is the CEO and founder of Kaushalya UK, an impactful voluntary community organization championing women’s confidence, resilience, and social inclusion. A qualified educator, author, and speaker, she established the annual Mental Health and Domestic Abuse Awareness Conference and earned multiple national accolades for her compassionate leadership and community advocacy.
fullText:
Ritu Sharma is an accomplished and visionary leader whose dedication to empowering women has created lasting change. She found and leads Kaushalya UK, (www.kaushalyauk.com) a voluntary community organisation that successfully designs and implements a range of initiatives aimed at enhancing confidence, resilience, and social inclusion among women from diverse backgrounds. Her flagship event, “Mental Health and Domestic Abuse Awareness Conference” has been running for three years and continues to receive exceptional feedback from participants, other local community organisations, partners and service users.
Her leadership is characterised by compassion, innovation, and strategic vision. Ritu’s background includes extensive experience in education as a qualified teacher, public speaking, not-for-profit management, creative writing, and community engagement — skills that she integrates seamlessly into her work. Her ability to motivate, communicate, and connect authentically with people from all walks of life is one of her defining strengths. She is also a published author, poet, and playwright, using storytelling as a powerful tool for healing and empowerment.
Ritu’s achievements have been widely recognised. Over the years, she has received several awards and honours acknowledging her contribution to women’s empowerment, community development, and leadership excellence. These include Empowerment Champion of the Year 2024, Finalist Local Heroes Award 2024, Annual Women Economic Forum Award winner 2023, Finalist Birmingham Awards 2023, Milestone Global Award 2022, International Women Icon Award 2022, India Star Republic Award 2022, Finalist Signature Awards (Birmingham) 2022, Extraordinary Achievers Award 2022, Finalist Women’s Business Awards 2021, International Women’s Inspirational Award 2021, Global Choice Award 2021, WOW Award Winner 2020, India Star Independent Award 2020, She Inspires Award 2020.
As the CEO of Kaushalya UK, Ritu has shown exceptional proficiency in strategic planning, project delivery, and partnership development. She manages multi-stakeholder collaborations with skill and integrity, ensuring that all projects are delivered to the highest standard. Her aptitude for securing funding, developing effective programmes, and leading teams with empathy has enabled Kaushalya UK to grow steadily and establish itself as a trusted and respected organisation in the voluntary sector.
Ritu Sharma is not only a leader but also an inspiration. Her authenticity, dedication, and unwavering belief in the power of women to shape their own futures have touched countless lives. She leads with both heart and intellect, blending business acumen with a humanitarian spirit that uplifts everyone she works with.
In summary, Ritu Sharma is an outstanding leader, changemaker, and advocate for women’s empowerment. Her professional accomplishments, creative talents, and award-winning contributions to community well-being make her an exemplary figure in the social impact field.

name: Rose Marok
org: Birmingham Mind Volunteer / Roshni Brand Ambassador
summary: Rose Marok is a dedicated community volunteer with Birmingham Mind and Brand Ambassador for Roshni Birmingham. She leads campaigns addressing domestic abuse prevention, cancer research, and mental wellbeing, establishing supportive community circles where women openly discuss emotional challenges and build personal resilience.
fullText: Driven by a lifelong commitment to service, Rose Marok has dedicated much of her time to supporting vulnerable individuals and strengthening communities. As a volunteer with Birmingham Mind and Brand Ambassador for Roshni Birmingham, she advocates for mental health, domestic abuse prevention, food poverty relief, and cancer research. Through her women’s empowerment platform, she creates safe and supportive spaces where women are encouraged to share their stories, speak openly about their experiences, build confidence, and prioritise their emotional wellbeing. Through fundraising, community outreach, awareness campaigns, and direct support services, she has helped create opportunities for empowerment, inclusion, and hope. Her humanitarian work reflects a deep belief that lasting change begins with compassion, action, and a commitment to serving others.

name: Mrs Sabitha Nalli
summary: Mrs Sabitha Nalli has served for over 10 years as Deputy Head of the Community School, educating over 600 students in their mother tongue and cultural traditions. In Milton Keynes, she has provided six years of free Bharatanatyam dance training to underprivileged youth and led virtual classes during lockdowns.
fullText: Sabitha Nalli has dedicated over 10 years as Deputy Head of the Community School, helping more than 600 students learn their mother tongue while preserving our culture, traditions, and values. In Milton Keynes, for the past six years, she has provided free Bharatanatyam training to students facing financial hardship and organised free online dance workshops during COVID-19, inspiring and supporting our community through her selfless service.

name: Sana Kardar
org: Biomedical Science / Women’s Health & Public Service
summary: Sana Kardar is a biomedical researcher and UK parliamentary advisor working across policy, women's health, and youth empowerment. An Imperial College MSc graduate and former national squash player, she established a 10,000-member support network for women with endometriosis and has dedicated over seven years to mentoring young people through PINE and Seeds of Peace.
fullText:
I am a biomedical scientist, researcher, educator and public service professional whose work sits at the intersection of science, policy, women’s health and community engagement. I hold a First Class Honours degree in Biomedical Sciences and completed my MSc in Bioscience Futures at Imperial College London with Distinction, where my work explored how scientific evidence and innovation can be translated into meaningful societal impact.
Professionally, I work within the UK Parliament, supporting the constituency office of Mohammad Yasin MP across policy, communications, community engagement and constituency matters. Alongside this, I contribute to teaching, mentoring and policy engagement, including at Imperial College London, where I have been invited to teach on policy and communication.
A significant thread throughout my journey has been creating opportunities for others, particularly women and young people. I have spent several years mentoring and supporting young people through education, leadership and community initiatives, while my advocacy in women’s health has focused on raising awareness, improving understanding and ensuring that experiences too often overlooked are represented in research and public conversations.
Before entering science and public service, I competed in squash at national level, an experience that shaped my understanding of discipline, resilience and the importance of opening opportunities for women and girls. Across science, sport, education and public life, I have tried to use the opportunities I have received to create space, visibility and opportunity for others.

name: Sandhya
summary: Sandhya is the Founder and Director of India Island Academy, an arts organization created to nurture cultural heritage, discipline, and self-esteem among youth. A dedicated single mother, she built the academy to teach classical Indian dance, music, and regional languages, providing young people and women platforms to perform on national and international stages.
fullText:
I am Sandhya Aaytee, a single mother of two children, the Founder and Director of India Island Academy, and someone who has always believed in turning challenges into opportunities to make a positive difference in the lives of others.
My journey to where I am today has not been easy. As a single parent, I have faced many personal and professional challenges while raising my two children and building India Island Academy from the ground up. There have been times when balancing motherhood, responsibilities and my vision for the Academy has been incredibly difficult, but those experiences have made me stronger, more determined and more compassionate towards others facing their own challenges.
India Island Academy began with my passion for Indian culture and desire for bringing up my children with Indian values in the Western country and ensure that our rich heritage continues to be valued and passed on to future generations. What started as a vision has grown into a vibrant community organisation, providing children and adults with opportunities to learn and celebrate Indian dance, music, languages and traditions, while also developing confidence, discipline and a sense of belonging.
For me, this journey has never been solely about building an organisation. It has been about creating opportunities for others, especially women & skilled individuals whilst bringing communities together and empowering women & young people through culture and the Arts. I am proud of how far I have come, particularly knowing the challenges I have overcome along the way, and I hope my journey can inspire other women and single mums to believe that their circumstances do not have to define their future.

name: Sangeeta Pandey
summary: Sangeeta Pandey combines experience in broadcast media and international entrepreneurship to support emerging professionals. She delivers cross-cultural executive coaching and training for enterprises navigating UK-India business relationships, alongside managing her family business in London and championing cultural understanding within professional networks.
fullText: Sangeeta has a background with the electronic media before setting up her business.. Coaching and mentoring she has offered numerous training sessions to individuals and groups in managing cultural challenges of cross border business especially within the UK India context. Currently she also manages her family run food business in London.

She leads workshops on traditional Ayurvedic maternal and postnatal care for doulas, preserving India's ancient holistic wellness knowledge across the UK.
fullText:
Dr Seema Datta – Community Service & Cultural Heritage
For many years, Dr Seema Datta has been committed to sharing India’s traditional wisdom of Ayurveda and supporting community wellbeing in the UK. As a volunteer with One Vision, Watford, she has contributed to preventive healthcare through community blood pressure screenings and supported unpaid carers. She has shared Ayurvedic knowledge of pregnancy, childbirth and postnatal care through community workshops for doulas, helping those who support mothers and families. She has also represented Ayurveda at The Mentor Ring’s South Asian Heritage Month celebrations, promoting awareness of India’s traditional healthcare heritage. Through these voluntary initiatives, she continues to contribute to healthier communities, women’s empowerment and the preservation of Indian wisdom for future generations.

name: Shalini Saxena
summary: Shalini Saxena is a London-based IT professional with more than two decades of technology experience who dedicates her expertise to charitable causes. For over eight years, she has provided complimentary web development, digital design, and ongoing technical maintenance to community initiatives and non-profits, including the LOANI Foundation and Family Mediation Service.
fullText:
I am Shalini Saxena, a London-based IT professional with over 20 years of experience in technology and digital solutions. I strongly believe in using my knowledge and skills to make a positive difference in society.
For the past eight years, I have been actively supporting charitable organisations, community initiatives and individuals by providing free digital and technical assistance. My passion lies in empowering others through technology, particularly those who may not have the resources or technical knowledge to access professional support.
I believe that true community service is not only about financial donations, but also about generously sharing our time, knowledge and skills to help others grow and succeed.

name: Shivali Ruparelia
org: Sai School of Harrow / Diwali in London
summary: Shivali Ruparelia is a Trustee of the Sai School of Harrow, dedicating every Saturday to voluntary youth education. She has managed stage and backstage operations for major cultural spectacles at the Royal Albert Hall and Wembley Arena, while coordinating charitable distributions of food and gifts to foster care facilities across North West London.
fullText: For several years, I have been actively involved in bringing communities together through culture, volunteering and service. I want my children to grow up understanding the importance of kindness, compassion and selfless service, and to be inspired to carry these values forward for generations to come.

Shraddha Ballal is a passionate community leader, social changemaker and accomplished Enterprise Architect with over 21 years of professional experience across diverse industries, including public sector, pharmaceuticals, retail, insurance and energy.
As the Co-founder of Namaste Kingston CIC, a volunteer-led, not-for-profit organisation, Shraddha is dedicated to fostering community cohesion, celebrating cultural diversity and creating meaningful connections. Through cultural festivals, health and wellbeing initiatives, charitable fundraising and collaborations with local organisations, she has helped build an inclusive platform that empowers communities, supports local businesses and promotes social impact.
Driven by the belief that meaningful change begins with people, Shraddha combines strategic leadership with grassroots action, bridging the worlds of business, culture and community to create lasting positive impact.

name: Silpa Paruchuri
summary: Silpa Paruchuri is the founder of Eastenders Women’s Group, providing 13 years of continuous community care, domestic abuse crisis guidance, and employment support for women. fullText:
I am the Founder of the Eastenders Women’s Group, established 13 years ago with a vision to bring women together through care, compassion, friendship, and mutual support. My journey has been guided by a strong belief in empowering women, building meaningful connections, and creating a community where every woman feels heard, valued, and encouraged to achieve her potential.

Through my community involvement and charitable initiatives, I remain committed to making a positive difference in people's lives and fostering a spirit of unity, kindness, and service.

name: Sonal Dave
summary: Sonal Dave has served 22 years as an adult court Magistrate (JP) since her appointment in 2004, inspiring diverse community members to pursue civic justice roles. She is also a long-standing member of Shishukunj, a London children's charity cultivating character, values, and community leadership in young people.
fullText: Sonal was appointed as a Magistrate (JP) in 2004, and since then has been listening to cases relating to adult crime, in the adult courts. Over her 22 years she has inspired others to apply to become magistrates and also talked about her role in communities. Sonal is also a member of Shishukunj, a children’s charity that has been working in London for over 50 years. The organisation instils good morals and values in children from the age of 5 upwards guiding and supporting them to be responsible and respected leaders of tomorrow’s society.

name: Sonia Gupta
summary: Sonia Gupta is a community advocate dedicated to dismantling divorce stigma, challenging cultural expectations, and fostering emotional wellbeing within South Asian communities. Since 2021, she has provided complimentary mentoring and heartfelt guidance to individuals navigating marital separation and personal adversity, empowering those struggling in silence to find their voice.
fullText: Since 2021, Sonia Gupta has dedicated her time to raising awareness of divorce stigma, cultural expectations and emotional wellbeing, particularly within South Asian communities. Having experienced years of family and societal pressure herself, she understands the importance of giving others a voice. Through voluntary mentoring, free guidance and emotional support, she has helped women and men navigating difficult relationships, separation and personal challenges, often giving her time without charge. By openly challenging cultural taboos and encouraging conversations that were once considered shameful, Sonia continues to create awareness, empower individuals and remind those struggling in silence that they are not alone.

name: Sonoo Malkani
summary: Sonoo Malkani has served the diverse communities of Harrow as a volunteer community leader for 49 years, working with the Local Authority, the Met Police, the London Mayor’s Office and faith groups. She has supported Met policing at a senior level for 27 years and is a former Chair of Harrow Interfaith and Harrow Carers.
fullText:
Dedicated Volunteer Community Leader, tirelessly serving diverse communities of Harrow since 49 years, collaborating with Local Authority, Met Police, London Mayor’s Office and Faith groups. Also promoting Community Cohesion & Racial harmony policing passionately helping deliver one of London’s safest boroughs.

27 years supporting challenging Met policing at Senior level.

Deeply religious former Chair Harrow Interfaith and Harrow Carers, with experienced in NHS equality issues plus awareness raising.

Fiercely patriotic Indian, equally proud Briton, adores engaging closely with and being the voice of the people to help develop trust and confidence. Loved living here since 1970. Feel privileged to serve.

name: Sridevi Meenavalli
summary: Sridevi Meenavalli is a data science professional and founder of Telugu Ladies in UK (TLUK), an organization she started in 2011 that now supports over 6,000 members. She provides domestic abuse signposting, funds educational degrees for disadvantaged students in India, and hosts health awareness and emotional resilience initiatives.
fullText:
I am Sridevi Meenavalli, a full-time IT professional specialising in Data Science and the founder of Telugu Ladies in UK (TLUK), established in 2011. My journey in community service began 15 years ago with a desire to address the isolation many Telugu women experience when leaving their homeland to build a new life in the UK. As a new mother living far from my family, I understood the importance of having a support network that shares your language, culture and experiences. This inspired me to create a community where Telugu-speaking women could find friendship, understanding and a sense of belonging with others navigating similar journeys.
What began as a small initiative has grown into one of the largest Telugu women’s communities in the UK and one of the early Indian women-led community groups in the country. Today, TLUK connects nearly 6,000 members through its private Facebook group, alongside a growing Instagram presence of 4000+ women and hundreds of women across its WhatsApp communities. Beyond its online reach, TLUK has become a home away from home, helping women build meaningful friendships, access community support and remain connected to their Telugu language, culture and heritage.
Alongside my full-time career, I am committed to empowering women, supporting girls’ education, raising awareness of domestic abuse, helping underprivileged students and promoting women’s physical and mental wellbeing. For me, TLUK is about transforming the shared challenges of life away from home into collective strength, compassion and meaningful community action. My journey is guided by one simple belief: when women lift each other up, they can transform not only individual lives but entire communities.

name: Sudha Kapashi
org: Mahavir Foundation Ladies Wing / Community Service
summary: Sudha Kapashi has dedicated decades to community welfare and cultural education. As founding President of the Mahavir Foundation Ladies Wing for nine years, she welcomed and guided newly arrived families from India. fullText:
I am very active in various organisations. Firstly I was helping Mahavir Foundation (MF) as a committee member and helped in organising big events. Then I was one of the founders of the Ladies Wing (under MF). I was the president of the Ladies Wing for about nine years. I organised many functions under the Ladies Wing. name: Sujatha Thaladi
org: The Mentor Ring / Royal Auxiliary Air Force
summary: Sujatha Thaladi is the Co-founder and CEO of The Mentor Ring, a registered charity providing comprehensive mentoring across education, careers, healthcare, and community integration throughout South East London, Kent, and Wales. An Organic Chemistry post-graduate, glider pilot, and Honorary Air Commodore of the Royal Auxiliary Air Force, she also chairs Centrepieces and Aurav Disha, dedicating over 17 years to uplifting marginalized groups and fostering cohesion.
fullText: Sujatha Thaladi is a postgraduate in Organic Chemistry, former lecturer in India, Rotarian, social entrepreneur, mentor, yoga tutor, and community leader. She is the Co-founder and CEO of The Mentor Ring, a registered charity in England and Wales dedicated to mentoring in the areas of education, careers, health and wellbeing, digital inclusion, and community cohesion. She serves communities across South East London, Kent, and Wales, organising events and initiatives that bring people together, foster community cohesion, and celebrate diversity. Sujatha is Chair of Centrepieces, a charity that supports mental health recovery through art-based activities. She is also Chair of Aurav Disha (A Direction of Peaceful Echo of Multicultural Wales) and Regional Coordinator for Wales for the South Asian Heritage Trust. In addition, she serves as the Honorary Air Commodore of No. 614 Squadron Royal Auxiliary Air Force. She is passionate about empowering people, promoting Indian culture and heritage, strengthening communities, and creating opportunities for people from all backgrounds to connect, learn, and thrive together.

name: Mrs Sulochana Sethi
summary: Mrs Sulochana Sethi has dedicated over twenty years to voluntary community service, establishing Vedicca London in 2012 to enrich the lives of senior citizens. Her organization provides weekly wellness workshops, digital literacy classes, and interfaith fellowship, alongside supporting vulnerable families with food and winter supplies.
fullText:
I have always believed that true service lies in making a meaningful difference to the lives of others, however small the gesture.
For over two decades, I have devoted my time to community service, particularly supporting the physical, emotional, social and spiritual wellbeing of older people. My guiding belief is that everyone, regardless of age or background, deserves to feel valued, connected and purposeful.
In 2012, I helped establish Vedicca London, a charity dedicated to enriching the lives of older adults. As President, I have seen it grow into a vibrant community of over 100 members. Through wellbeing programmes, social and cultural activities, educational workshops and outings, we encourage friendship, confidence and active participation. What gives me particular joy is seeing members move beyond simply attending activities to sharing their own talents, skills and experiences, becoming contributors to the community themselves.
My voluntary service also includes supporting vulnerable families through food distribution, winter warmth initiatives, blood donation drives and community partnerships. For over 20 years, I have been associated with Sachkhand Nanak Dham, promoting compassion, spiritual wellbeing and harmony across faiths. During COVID-19, every week, to stop people feeling isolated and low, I continued to run our club online for our members; and also a bhajan sandhya session every week to which the wider community was invited. Everyone was encouraged to learn to use zoom, to come dressed as if they were going out. It was heart warming to see our attendance rise from 20 to over 100 with families and couples attending and various professional musicians calling to volunteer their services.
I firmly believe that age should never be a barrier to purpose, participation or joy, and that service has no retirement age.
My greatest reward is seeing someone who once felt isolated rediscover friendship, confidence and a sense of belonging. If my journey inspires others to give their time, share their skills or extend a helping hand, I consider that a meaningful achievement.

name: Sunita Chaubey
summary: With over 25 years of professional experience in the UK, she has always believed in empowering women and giving back to her community. She has been working hard to promote the rich Purvanchal culture, language, and traditions.
fullText:
With over 25 years of professional experience in the UK, she has always believed in empowering women and giving back to her community.

She has been working hard to promote the rich Purvanchal culture, language, and traditions, creating platforms through cultural events where women can showcase their hidden talents and shine with confidence.

Alongside this, she takes pride in coaching, mentoring, and motivating women returning to work after career breaks, helping them rebuild confidence and achieve financial independence. name: Suparna Rathi
summary: Suparna Rathi is a certified leadership coach and the Founder and Chair of HerShakti, a free women’s empowerment community offering mindset, self-awareness, and personal growth circles. She also established Yummy Indian Ladies in Hounslow, organizing cultural celebrations that foster inclusion and community belonging.
fullText: Suparna is the Founder and Chair of HerShakti, a free women’s empowerment community she runs as her “heart work.” A certified leadership coach, she gives her professional skills freely — running monthly circles and online sessions that guide women through mindset and self-awareness, from boundaries and self-worth to identity, fear patterns and people-pleasing, at no cost and open to all. She also founded Yummy Indian Ladies, a grassroots women’s community in Hounslow, and brings people together through multicultural events celebrating culture, connection and belonging. Her belief is simple: every woman deserves to feel seen, supported and empowered — and community is built by showing up, consistently and generously, for one another.

name: Surinder Kenth
org: Voice of Women Club / Cultural Celebrations
summary: Surinder Kenth has delivered over 14 years of charitable community service, focusing on Punjabi heritage and female empowerment. She directs the Voice of Women club, providing a welcoming environment for mutual support and personal development. She also coordinates annual Teeyan and Diwali festivals, bringing diverse communities together through music, giddha dance, and shared traditions.
fullText: For over 14 years I have been committed to charitable community service in the UK. I run an annual Teeyan event to celebrate Punjabi culture and bring women together through giddha, music, and friendship. I also organise Diwali events to promote our traditions and spread joy in the community. Additionally, I run the Voice of Women club, which supports and uplifts women by giving them a platform to connect, share, and grow. All of this work is voluntary and non-commercial, with the aim of strengthening community bonds and empowering women.

name: Sushma Bhanot MBE
org: Integrative Medicine / The Great British Chai Party
summary: Sushma Bhanot MBE is a pharmacist, author, and pioneer in natural integrative medicine and botanical healthcare. She has trained 6,000 women in integrative health, runs free clinics for vulnerable women, and co-founded The Great British Chai Party to combat elderly isolation, earning an MBE for services to wellness and community.
fullText:
Sushma Bhanot MBE Pharmacist ,Integrative Medicine, homoeopath, lecturer, author, philanthropist,
Sushma Bhanot has transformed the landscape of Natural Health. She has trained 6000 women in integrative health and beauty and pioneering Ayurveda in the Uk. She has formulated and launched her own award winning skincare and Hair care range based on ayurvedic botanicals. She is co -author of 2 influential books and a mentor too dedicated to helping women gain skills confidence and financial
Independence. Her mission to lift others as she rises.She also runs free integrative health wellbeing clinics for vunerable women .
Sushma is a Co-Founder of The Great British Chai Party Charity, a charity to help tackle loneliness and social isolation within our growing aged population She is also a Co-Founder and Trustee of Make it Beat Charity. Patron of Binti International which stands for menstrual dignity in women.
Sushma was recently recognized for 'Outstanding Service to Promote Health & Wellness in the UK, the Global Woman Wellness Leadership award. Recently was selected to be on the cover of lifestyle and health magazine Luxurist.
Her dedication has earned her one of the country’s highest honours - an MBE - member of the British Empire by the Queen .Watch this space for her next initiative launching soon for women’s mental wellbeing.

name: Sushmita Pati
summary: Sushmita Pati is an award-winning Odissi and Kathak choreographer, ethnomusicologist, and Artistic Director of Kala The Arts. For over 35 years, she has championed South Asian classical dance across the UK, introducing Indian arts to 418 schools, curating museum exhibitions, and leveraging movement arts to enhance mental health and wellbeing among disadvantaged children.
fullText: An award winning international choreographer in classical dance kathak and Odissi, an ethnomusicologist, a trailblazer in introducing India through arts and culture in Hampshire region. Introduced Indian culture and dance forms to 418 schools in Hampshire and Berkshire. Worked with Mira Mishra Kaushik at Akademi London, Odissi examiner for Bhavan and founder member of Kala The Arts arts in education charit and a women lead organisation . Supported artists mostly women empowering them to develop their career in Dance over the period of 35 years and works with local, national and international museums to curate Indian arts in their gallery and deepen understanding of Indian arts. Works with disadvantaged children and families and creates programmes where they connect with arts and improve mental health. Continues to research how arts improves mental health for all in society and in particular ethnic women and Indian women . She is invited to give talks at various local and international platform. She is a great leader and a visionary leader.

name: Sutapa Ray
summary: Sutapa Ray is an educator, neurodiversity advocate, and co-founder of Sangeet Foundation, a registered charity utilizing music and arts to tackle mental health stigma and support individuals with ADHD, anxiety, and dyspraxia across India and the UK, including collaborative policy programmes at the House of Commons.
fullText: Sutapa Ray is an educator, mental health and neurodiversity advocate, and co-founder of Sangeet Foundation, a charity for addressing mental health and neurodiversity using music and the arts. With nearly 20 years’ teaching experience across India and the UK, she inspires students, especially those facing barriers, through inclusive, innovative support. Drawing on her family’s lived experience of ADHD, anxiety and dyspraxia, she has used music and the arts to challenge stigma within South Asian communities. Through Sangeet Foundation, she has led awareness programmes, workshops, research partnerships with universities, and collaborations with NHS charities, NGOs and policymakers, including at the House of Commons. Sutapa’s work builds understanding, hope and access to support.

name: Swagatika Patra
org: Financial Conduct Authority / Pattachitra Arts & Mentorship
summary: Swagatika Patra works in financial regulation and artificial intelligence at the FCA, while actively promoting women's empowerment and traditional Indian art. An ambassador for international women's forums, she mentors emerging female professionals and showcases traditional Odia Pattachitra art globally, earning the GlobalWIIN Special Recognition Award in 2025.
fullText:
I work at the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) in the UK and have a strong interest in artificial intelligence and how technology can support positive change. Alongside my professional career, I am passionate about women’s empowerment, inclusion, mental health awareness and helping women gain confidence and recognition.
My community work includes independently mentoring women in India, raising awareness of women’s mental health through published articles, and supporting the visibility of women Pattachitra artists from Odisha by promoting their artwork. I am involved with UN Women UK and G100 and have also contributed to the Global Queens women’s platform. My work brings together women’s empowerment, cultural heritage and the belief that women can create greater opportunities for one another when they work together.

name: Sweta Mohanty
org: Jammu & Kashmir Study Centre UK / Cultural Diplomacy
summary: Sweta Mohanty has spent eight years promoting nuanced international policy dialogue and UK-India cultural diplomacy. Leading efforts at the Jammu & Kashmir Study Centre UK, she organizes evidence-based public symposia to counter misinformation. She has also pioneered major showcases of Odia maritime history and arts, including the inaugural Bali Jatra celebration at the UK Parliament.
fullText:
Over the past several years, Sweta has developed a broad network spanning diaspora organisations, parliamentarians, policymakers, academics, business leaders, faith communities and international institutions. Her work focuses on creating platforms for dialogue, strengthening people-to-people connections and developing opportunities for deeper institutional and economic engagement between India, the UK and the wider international community
● Jammu & Kashmir Strategic Outreach — JKSC UK: As a UK-based leader within Jammu Kashmir Study Centre UK, Sweta has contributed to developing the organisation as a platform for informed engagement on Jammu & Kashmir through research, publications, media engagement, parliamentary events and international outreach. In 2026, she participated in a people-to-people delegation to Israel, including senior-level engagements with Amichai Chikli, Israel’s Minister for Diaspora Affairs, and MK Ohad Tal.
● India Narratives & Public Discourse — FISI UK: As a key Executive Member of Friends of India Society International UK, Sweta contributes to communications, research, events and public engagement. For FISI UK’s 50th anniversary in 2026, she led the curation of its historical archives, conceptualised an exhibition documenting the organisation’s five-decade journey, served as Editor of its Golden Jubilee publication, and moderated a panel discussion at an event attended by more than 350 members and guests..
● International Outreach & Institutional Dialogue: Sweta has been part of the core team involved in conceptualising and coordinating international outreach with UK parliamentarians, faith leaders, academics and community leaders, facilitating dialogue and greater understanding around India and its global engagement. This work has included supporting engagements with senior Indian and RSS leaders, including Smriti Irani, Dattatreya Hosabale and Dr Mohan Bhagwat, as part of wider international outreach initiatives.
Promoting Odisha, its Development & Diaspora Engagement
Sweta is a Core Committee Member of the Odisha Society of United Kingdom CIC, where she plays an active role in building a meaningful “living bridge” between Odisha and the United Kingdom. Her work focuses on raising Odisha’s profile in the UK, strengthening institutional and people-to-people connections, to support Odisha’s economic, educational, tourism, cultural and broader developmental aspirations.
● Global South Maritime Heritage Summit & Bali Jatra UK 2025: Key Executive Member involved in leading the Global South Maritime Heritage Summit at the UK Parliament, highlighting Odisha’s maritime heritage and the global significance of Bali Jatra. Served as spokesperson for Bali Jatra UK 2025, including media engagement and NDTV coverage.
● Diaspora & Investment Engagement: Mobilised UK Odia diaspora participation in Pravasi Bharatiya Divas Odisha 2025, linking diaspora expertise and networks with development and investment opportunities in Odisha. Appointed by the High Commission of India as lead coordinator for the diaspora interaction with External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar in January 2025.
● Nabarangpur Development & International Opportunities: Participated in an international delegation to Nabarangpur, Odisha, exploring opportunities to convert agricultural waste into energy and engaging with local communities to understand the potential economic and environmental benefits.Toured the district alongside the local MLA and district administration to explore its tourism potential and identify opportunities to position Nabarangpur for greater national and international visibility.
● International Advocacy & Odisha-Born Leadership: Conceived and organised a UK Parliament event in May 2026 showcasing the international work of an Odisha-born global campaigner for paid period leave, bringing together an international audience and highlighting Odisha-origin leadership and social innovation on a global platform.
Current Focus
Sweta is currently focused on identifying and developing high-quality, scalable opportunities in Odisha, particularly at the intersection of tourism, wellness, education, skills, culture, infrastructure and international engagement.
Her broader objective is to contribute to Odisha’s emergence as a destination for international investment, talent, knowledge, tourism and enterprise, while creating commercially sustainable opportunities that connect the state with global networks.

summary: Usha Raghavan is an internationally acclaimed Bharatanatyam dancer, choreographer, and Founder-Director of Kalasagara UK. Living in London since 1996, she has organized international dance marathons and relief drives for disaster relief and blind welfare centres, while curating cultural heritage tours for aspiring UK dancers.

name: Vandana Khurana
org: NHS Transformation / Vedic Cultural Society of East Anglia
summary: Vandana Khurana is an NHS transformation consultant, voluntary Hindu chaplain, author, and humanitarian. As Founder and Chair of the Vedic Cultural Society of East Anglia, she has built vital interfaith and cultural bridges across Norfolk. Her literary work 'The Legacy of Hanuman Chalisa' earned a World Book Record at Parliament, complemented by decades of hospital chaplaincy and charitable broadcasting.
fullText: Born and brought up in India joined my husband in UK after marriage in 1993. I’m a proud mother of three children, based in coastal village Hopton, Norfolk UK for last 28 years . I embarked upon my career after my children went full time education and I’m humbled as well proud to be a UK-based leading business consultant serving the NHS, founder and chair of the Vedic Cultural Society of East Anglia, voluntary Hindu chaplain, global literary chair, award-winning author, and humanitarian. Honoured with the World Book Record 2024 at the Houses of Parliament, London, for The Legacy of Hanuman Chalisa, and recipient of the Citation for Community Spirit 2026, feel grateful to be celebrated for my outstanding contributions to healthcare leadership, community service, cultural preservation, interfaith harmony, women’s empowerment, charitable broadcasting, and international literary collaboration that brings diverse cultures together through poetry, dialogue, and shared human values. I’m humbled and grateful to be recognised as inspiring leader by community with compassion and humane values. I truly appreciate platform set by Rashmi Mishra in UK to pioneer and recognise women contribution to society and make them feel empowered. I feel there is lots of work we all can do together to support and appreciate each other in this journey of life . “Promises yet to be kept still shine like stars above, And I will keep moving forward, serving society with strength and love.”

name: Varsha
org: UKAWC & Harrow Council / Community Leadership & Voluntary Service
summary: Varsha has dedicated over three decades to voluntary service across New Zealand, Qatar, and the UK. Honored with Harrow Council’s Lifetime Achievement and Mayor’s awards, she leads UKAWC supporting Asian women, volunteers for talking newspapers for the blind, and organizes community initiatives including Pinner Deepawali and Cuppa and Catchup.
fullText:
Varsha’s journey in voluntary work has shaped her life and changed the meaning of how much she thought was possible to give back to the community.
She began her voluntary work in Wellington, New Zealand, continued it in Doha, Qatar then brought it to London 31 years ago. Her numerous voluntary roles have taught her valuable lessons in how to empower individuals and strengthen communities.
In the UK, she worked tirelessly with different charities including mental health charities and Mencap. She now dedicates herself to volunteering for a talking newspaper for the blind, leading a walking team for the Harrow council and runs UKAWC, an organisation committed to working with Asian women.
She was awarded the Lifetime Achievement award by the Harrow Council, received a Community Leadership Award and was presented with an award by the Worshipful The Mayor of Harrow for Exceptional & Standing dedication to voluntary service.
Other projects she’s involved in include organising Deepawali in the Pinner Memorial Park and a new community services called Cuppa and Catchup aimed at bringing the local community together.
She is proud to be supported and loved by her husband, children and friends. Varsha’s motto is “Help out and give back to the community, no matter how small the deed.”

name: Vidhi Bhagat
summary: Vidhi Bhagat has provided more than seven years of voluntary community seva in Bradford through yoga education, cultural camps, and youth sports. She leads donation-funded yoga sessions with proceeds benefiting local temples, directs children’s creative arts and wellness retreats, and coaches Under-11 cricket to empower young girls and promote healthy, active lifestyles.
fullText:
I am Vidhi Bhagat from Bradford, UK. For the past 7+ years I have been dedicated to community seva through yoga and dance , art and craft to kids and ladies .
I voluntarily teach yoga , conduct donation-based yoga classes at the temple with proceeds going to the temple,
and run Kids Arts, Crafts, Yoga & Dance camps to promote culture and wellbeing among children.
I also coach Under-11 girls cricket to encourage young girls in sports.
My work focuses on uplifting women, children and community through health, culture and selfless service.
